title: Repurposing amlodipine, fluoxetine, and escitalopram as non-antibiotic adjuvants: in vitro enhancement of ciprofloxacin and fluconazole activity against multidrug-resistant bacterial and candida clinical isolates.
abstract: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Candida albicans threaten treatment success, particularly in resource-limited settings. Repurposing licensed, inexpensive non-antibiotic drugs may provide a strategy for enhancing the activity of established antimicrobial agents. Clinical isolates from Sana'a, Yemen, and American Type Culture Collection (ATCC) reference strains were tested in vitro with amlodipine, fluoxetine, and escitalopram, individually and in dual or triple combinations with ciprofloxacin or fluconazole. Antimicrobial activity was evaluated using agar-well diffusion, broth microdilution minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), minimum bactericidal or fungicidal concentration (MBC/MFC), and checkerboard fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI) assays. Molecular docking with AutoDock Vina was used to explore plausible interactions with MurB (PDB 1HSK), LasR (PDB 3IX3), and CYP51 (PDB 5V5Z). Normal mode analysis (NMA) with iMODS was performed for selected fluoxetine-LasR and fluoxetine-MurB complexes as a preliminary structural-dynamics assessment. Fluoxetine produced inhibition zones of at least 27 mm across the tested organisms. Amlodipine produced larger zones against S. aureus and C. albicans than against P. aeruginosa, whereas escitalopram produced smaller zones overall. Checkerboard testing identified synergy (FICI ≤ 0.50) for selected combinations. Selected triple combinations reduced MIC values by 4- to 64-fold. The largest diffusion readouts were observed with ciprofloxacin + fluoxetine + amlodipine against S. aureus (101 mm), ciprofloxacin + fluoxetine + escitalopram against P. aeruginosa (88.5 mm), and ciprofloxacin + amlodipine + fluconazole against C. albicans (138.5 mm). Docking scores and NMA outputs provided hypothesis-generating structural context for the experimental findings. Antimicrobial enhancement was combination- and organism-dependent. Selected combinations showed checkerboard-defined synergy, whereas diffusion assays were interpreted as screening outcomes only. Docking and NMA findings were supportive and hypothesis-generating but did not establish target engagement or mechanism.

title: Confronting stigma in neurogenetic diseases in Tanzania: a clinician - informed narrative.
abstract: Genetic diagnoses can reduce diagnostic uncertainty but may also intensify stigma, particularly where neurogenetic disorders carry strong social and spiritual meanings. In Tanzania, access to genetic testing remains limited, and diagnoses are often established through available testing combined with compelling clinical evidence. Grounded in the Health Stigma and Discrimination Framework and informed by clinical and research experience in Tanzania, this clinician-informed narrative examines stigma associated with neurogenetic disorders. The article identifies drivers, facilitators, intersecting stigmas, manifestations, and outcomes of stigma in neurogenetic conditions. It operationalizes the framework for low-resource settings and highlights how cultural beliefs, limited genetic literacy, health-system gaps, gender norms, disability stigma, and socioeconomic vulnerability can shape families' experiences. Context-sensitive strategies across clinical, institutional, and community levels are needed to mitigate stigma. Applying the framework can support more equitable, dignified, and culturally responsive neurogenetic care in Tanzania.

title: Cerebrospinal fluid positive for SARS-CoV-2 associated with neurological manifestations and proteome alterations in a multiple myeloma patient.
journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
abstract: Although SARS-CoV-2 infection is primarily associated with respiratory symptoms, neurological complications have been increasingly recognized, even in the absence of pulmonary involvement. We report a case of a 67-year-old woman with a history of multiple myeloma and recent exposure to a COVID-19-positive individual who developed rapidly progressive neurological symptoms, including dysarthria, dysphagia, and hypoesthesia, without any respiratory manifestations. Her condition deteriorated to focal and dyscognitive status epilepticus, requiring mechanical ventilation. Brain MRI showed imaging features consistent with rhombencephalitis. SARS-CoV-2 infection was confirmed through positive qRT-PCR results from both nasopharyngeal swab and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Further analysis of the CSF using quantitative shotgun proteomics via mass spectrometry revealed a neuroinflammatory profile indicative of blood-brain barrier disruption and differential expression of several proteins relevant to brain function, including the major prion protein, superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD-1), and other aggregation-prone proteins. This case supports the hypothesis that SARS-CoV-2 can invade the central nervous system and cause severe neurological impairment, even in the absence of typical respiratory symptoms. The findings underscore the importance of considering SARS-CoV-2 in the differential diagnosis of rapidly progressive neurological syndromes and highlight the need for further investigation into the mechanisms of neuroinvasion and the potential neurotropism of emerging viral variants.

title: Exploring body image perception in people with multiple sclerosis: the role of self-esteem and disease burden.
journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) may affect physical functioning, self-perception, and psychosocial well-being. Although body image may be understood as a fundamental element of the psychological experience of people with MS (PwMS), it has not been sufficiently investigated in MS. This study aimed to explore body image perception and its contributors among PwMS. This cross-sectional study enrolled 100 PwMS from the Isfahan Hakim MS Database between November 2025 and March 2026. Data were collected using demographic and clinical questionnaires and validated Persian versions of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS), Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES), Multiple Sclerosis Impact Scale-29 (MSIS-29), and Patient Determined Disease Steps Scale (PDDS). The generalized linear model was applied to identify candidate predictors of body image in PwMS. PwMS were predominantly female (77%), with a mean age of 34.4 years, and most had relapsing-remitting MS (85%). In multivariable analyses, higher self-esteem consistently emerged as the strongest independent predictor of more favorable body image (B = 1.05, p < 0.001). Shorter disease duration (B = -0.02, p = 0.036), older age at disease onset (B = 0.12, p = 0.049), lower psychological impact (B = -0.18, p = 0.023), and lower overall MS impact (B = -0.06, p = 0.047) were also independently associated with better body image. Body image perception in PwMS is influenced by psychological resources and perceived disease burden, beyond neurological disability alone. Integrating interventions such as self-esteem-enhancing and psychologically supportive into MS care may improve patient-centered outcomes.

title: Craniovertebral junction injuries in children: a single center retrospective review.
journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
abstract: The craniovertebral junction is a unique structure consisting of the occipito-atlantal and atlanto-axial joints and their associated ligaments. The aim of the present study was to characterize the presentation, underlying mechanism of trauma, clinical and radiological findings, management, and outcome of children with craniovertebral junction injury treated in our institution. We undertook a retrospective review of all patients with craniovertebral junction injuries treated at our institution between January 2016 and June 2024. Craniovertebral junction injury was defined as presence of one or more of (i) bony fracture or dislocation of the occipital condyles and/or any part of the atlas or axis, (ii) atlanto-axial dislocation/subluxation identified as per standard radiological criteria as described in literature, (iii) ligamentous injury identified on MRI or instability identified on dynamic imaging, and (iv) spinal extra-axial and spinal parenchymal hemorrhage at the level of craniovertebral junction. Patients who had non-traumatic anomalies of the craniovertebral junction and who had incomplete records were excluded from the study. From 732 patients who underwent imaging evaluation at the emergency department for traumatic cervical spine injury, we identified 33 patients who met our inclusion criteria for craniovertebral junction injury. Motor vehicle accidents were the most common cause of injury, with the majority of patients suffering from ligamentous injury. Fractures of the occipital condyle were the most common bony injury of the craniovertebral junction. Most of the patients had good neurological outcomes, with mortality reported in 2/33. Multiple correspondence analysis identified a high-severity phenotype characterized by CVJ injury together with neurological and systemic compromise. An exploratory eight-item CVJ Injury Score was derived to characterize this phenotype. Craniovertebral junction injury in children is relatively rare, occurring in 4.5% of patients undergoing imaging evaluation for cervical spine injury in our series. It encompasses a broad clinical spectrum, ranging from injuries successfully managed non-operatively to severe injuries associated with neurological, vascular, and systemic physiological compromise. The proposed CVJ Injury Score represents an exploratory framework for characterizing this high-severity phenotype and requires external multicenter validation.

title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) combined with antidepressant pharmacotherapy for depression: state-dependent mechanisms, clinical evidence, and translational challenges.
abstract: Depression is a highly prevalent and debilitating mental disorder. Pharmacotherapy remains the primary treatment modality; however, its efficacy is often limited by a delayed onset of action, suboptimal response in some patients, and a high risk of recurrence. Treatment-resistant depression, characterized by poor response to conventional therapies, poses a major clinical challenge and highlights the need for improved treatment strategies. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), a noninvasive neuromodulation technique, has shown promise for depression, particularly when combined with antidepressant pharmacotherapy. Advances in neuroimaging, neurochemistry, and network neuroscience have clarified how high-frequency rTMS may modulate cortical excitability, monoaminergic transmission, synaptic plasticity, and distributed brain networks. Clinical evidence suggests that combined treatment may accelerate early improvement, increase response and remission, and reduce relapse risk; however, these benefits are heterogeneous across patients and symptom domains and should be interpreted in light of expectancy effects and limitations of sham blinding. Neuroimaging studies have identified treatment-associated functional and structural changes, including hippocampal volume changes, but the causal links among molecular signaling, circuit reorganization, structural findings, and symptom improvement remain unresolved. The interaction between rTMS and antidepressants should therefore not be viewed as uniformly additive or synergistic, but as a state-dependent process shaped by medication class, stimulation protocol and timing, cortical excitability, metaplasticity, and individual neurobiological context. This review integrates mechanistic, neuroimaging, and clinical evidence and discusses how biomarker-, state-, and symptom-informed targeting, optimized treatment sequencing, and pragmatic implementation strategies could improve the precision and accessibility of combined treatment for depression.

title: Oncogenic mutations in non-small cell lung cancer: from molecular mechanisms to clinical practice.
abstract: Targeted therapy has revolutionized the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients harboring oncogenic alterations, and next-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) significantly increase blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, leading to improved disease control and survival benefits. However, several issues remain to be addressed, including the selection of more appropriate and individualized agents, the emergence of TKI resistance, and the challenging management of central nervous system (CNS) progression. In this review, we comprehensively summarize the efficacy and safety of TKIs and targeted specific antibodies in advanced or metastatic patients with common or rare mutations, providing guidance in selecting the optimal agent. We further explore the mechanisms underlying drug resistance and regimens aimed at overcoming resistance. In nonmetastatic resectable or unresectable NSCLC, we discuss the therapeutic potential of targeted agents and current issues requiring further research. In addition, we distinguish current and potential therapeutic strategies for patients with baseline brain metastasis (BM) and those without baseline BM who subsequently develop brain progression, leading to more effective and personalized treatment. Finally, we provide perspectives on challenges and future directions in the identification and treatment of oncogenic alterations, particularly in the context of co-mutations and the heterogeneous nature of metastases, and emphasize the clinical importance of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted genetic testing and biomarker development.

title: Laminar architecture of a decision circuit in the mouse orbitofrontal cortex.
abstract: During economic choice, different neurons in orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) encode individual offer values, the binary choice outcome, and the chosen value. Previous work suggests that these cell groups form a decision circuit, but the anatomical organization of this circuit is poorly understood. Using calcium imaging, we recorded from layer 2/3 (L2/3) and layer 5 (L5) of mice choosing between different juice flavors offered in variable amounts. Decision variables were differentially represented across layers: juice-specific offer values and their spatial configuration were predominant in L2/3, while spatial offer values, chosen side, and chosen value were predominant in L5. Within each layer, functional cell groups were organized in clusters. The temporal dynamics of neural signals in the two layers indicated a combination of feed-forward and feed-back processes, and pointed to L5 as the locus for winner-take-all value comparison. These results reveal that economic decisions rely on a complex architecture distributed across layers of OFC.

title: Structure based discovery of antipsychotic-like TAAR1 agonists.
abstract: Schizophrenia is a severe mental illness whose current treatments primarily target dopamine and serotonin receptors. These drugs often cause side effects and vary in effectiveness across patients. The trace amine-associated receptor 1 (TAAR1), which modulates monoamine signaling, has emerged as a promising alternative target. To discover previously unexplored TAAR1 ligands, we computationally dock 65 million molecules against the active state of TAAR1 and experimentally test 55 of those highly ranked. Fourteen TAAR1 agonists emerge with potencies ranging from mid-nanomolar to micromolar. This high functional selectivity may reflect the compact conformation adopted by the activated TAAR1 orthosteric site. While this is favorable for agonist prioritization, simulations suggest that it can be over-optimized for initial hit rates at the expense of subsequent affinity maturation. Hit optimization yields nanomolar agonists whose docking-predicted poses are confirmed by cryo-EM. Three agonists have high brain exposure and potencies, with one compound showing potency comparable to the investigational drug ulotaront and two compounds exhibiting even greater potency, at levels sufficient for behavioral studies. All three potently normalize amphetamine-induced pre-pulse inhibition in mice, a model for schizophrenia, without catalepsy, a common side effect of traditional antipsychotics.

title: The paradox of high IQ in ADHD: dissociable effects on inattention and impulsivity - insights from behavior, cognition & brain in 5138 children.
abstract: While Intelligence Quotient (IQ) is widely considered a linear protective factor against attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), this paradigm fails to capture domain-specific nuances. We investigated whether non-linear relationships between IQ profiles and ADHD symptoms exist in a large cohort of children diagnosed with ADHD using a multidimensional dataset that integrates behavioral assessments, cognitive testing, and neuroimaging data. We examined a cohort of 5138 children aged 6-16 years diagnosed with ADHD, spanning a broad IQ range, and employed Restricted Cubic Spline (RCS) models to characterize the relationships between IQ measures [Full-Scale IQ (FIQ), Verbal IQ (VIQ), and Performance IQ (PIQ)] and core ADHD symptoms [Total scores, Inattention (IA), and hyperactivity/impulsivity subscales (H/IMP)]. This analytical framework was subsequently extended to executive function performance and brain surface area measurements to provide convergent mechanistic evidence. Latent Profile Analysis (LPA) was utilized to validate the non-linear relationship between functional impairments and IQ levels. FIQ demonstrated a linear negative association with total ADHD symptoms (β = -0.026, t = -3.27, p = 0.001). We identified a "double-edged sword" effect for IQ: while VIQ was linearly associated with lower IA scores (β = -0.015, t = -4.10, p < 0.001), it was associated with higher IMP scores (β = 0.007, t = 2.66, p = 0.008). Conversely, PIQ exhibited a dynamic developmental trajectory; the negative correlation between PIQ and IMP observed in childhood inverted into a significant U-shaped relationship in adolescence (p = 0.008). These behavioral findings were substantiated by convergent neuropsychological and neuroanatomical evidence. Finally, LPA validated a distinct "High IQ/High Impulsivity" subtype characterized by unique cognitive profiles. In conclusion, higher IQ appears to be associated with lower levels of inattention but greater impulsivity, potentially through distinct neurocognitive mechanisms. This refutes the model of IQ as a uniform protector and highlights the need to target inhibitory deficits, especially in high-IQ populations.

title: Characterizing gradients of functional connectome underpinning rumination and their alteration in depression.
abstract: As a prominent psychopathological process of major depressive disorder (MDD), rumination's brain underpinnings remain unclear. Emerging studies have highlighted that the brain is organized along several macroscale gradients, which could serve as a powerful framework for better understanding how the functional connectome underlies rumination. In this study, we leveraged two datasets (Rum-Beijing and Rum-MDD) to characterize the gradient structure during an active ruminative state. Rum-Beijing consisted of 40 healthy controls (HC) who underwent 3 repetitive scans, while Rum-MDD consisted of 45 patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) and 46 HCs. We used a modified rumination state task (RST) to induce participants into a continuous, active rumination state and investigated the gradient profiles. Several global features of the gradient (range, explanation ratio, variance) and the regional differences of each gradient were also compared. In the Rum-MDD dataset, we further examined the interaction effect between the group (MDD vs. HC) and condition (rumination vs. distraction) regarding the gradient's global and local metrics. Two gradients were identified: the primary-transmodal gradient and the visual-sensorimotor gradient. We found that the rumination state exhibited reduced gradient values in the default mode network (DMN) as compared to the distraction state. We identified replicable altered gradient values in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), superior frontal gyrus (SFG), and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC). Relative to the distraction state, individuals' gradient range exhibited a replicable and significant reduction along the primary-transmodal gradient, accompanied by a significant increase along the visual-sensorimotor gradient during rumination. Moreover, the MDD group showed a significantly higher primary-transmodal gradient range during the rumination state than HCs. In conclusion, the present study showed that rumination may correspond to a specific underlying functional gradient profile, which was altered in patients with MDD. These results shed new light on the neural mechanisms underlying rumination, highlighting a global functional coupling characteristic across the whole brain during active rumination.

title: Dual benefit of esketamine-based opioid-free anesthesia on postoperative pain and mental health outcomes in patients undergoing bariatric surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Patients with morbid obesity are at a high risk of comorbid depressive and anxiety symptoms. While bariatric surgery is an effective treatment, conventional opioid-based anesthesia carries significant perioperative risks. Opioid-free anesthesia (OFA) presents a safer alternative. Esketamine, known for its dual analgesic and rapid antidepressant effects, is a promising component of OFA. However, clinical evidence supporting its simultaneous benefits for both physical and psychological recovery in bariatric patients remains limited. In this double-blind, randomized clinical trial, patients scheduled for laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either esketamine-based anaesthesia or opioid-based anaesthesia with remifentanil during surgery. The co-primary outcomes were postoperative pain intensity within the first 24 h and mental health status at three months after surgery. Secondary outcomes included pharmacokinetics of esketamine and adverse events. A total of 84 patients were randomized, with 42 allocated to each group. Seventy-four participants (88.1%) completed the 3-month follow-up. Patients in the esketamine group experienced significantly lower postoperative pain intensity (P < 0.01) and a reduced incidence of moderate-to-severe pain (P < 0.05) within 24 h after surgery. Mental health outcomes at 3 months were also significantly better in the esketamine group, and adverse events rate did not differ significantly. Pharmacokinetic analysis showed that plasma esketamine concentrations increased rapidly during infusion, with early formation of the active metabolite (S)-norketamine. Compared to opioid-based anaesthesia, esketamine-based opioid-free anaesthesia was associated with improved postoperative analgesia and better mental health outcomes in morbidly obese patients undergoing bariatric surgery, without increasing adverse events.

title: Genetic architecture of MRI-derived cervical spinal cord morphology reveals sensory-motor axis and systemic disease associations.
abstract: The spinal cord is critical to motor, sensory, autonomic function, and increasingly implicated in neurological disease and human health, yet its genetic architecture remains largely unexplored. We perform large-scale phenotyping of the upper cervical spinal cord (C1-C3) structure using brain magnetic resonance imaging from over 80,000 UK Biobank participants, extracting shape metrics including cross-sectional area, diameters, and eccentricity. We identify a total of 179 independent genome-wide significant variants, with cervical spinal cord morphology showing moderate to high SNP-based heritability (0.16 to 0.42). We also uncover sex-specific genetic signals, highlighting potential biological sex differences in spinal cord development. In addition, spinal cord structure is associated with a wide range of neurological, metabolic, and systemic conditions, such as multiple sclerosis, neuropathies, diabetes, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. These findings establish the cervical spinal cord as a genetically informative and health relevant structure, offering opportunities to study its role in disease mechanisms and human health.

title: GSNO-functionalized hydroxyapatite nanofertilizer for prolonged delivery, detoxification, and yield improvement in maize.
abstract: The agricultural use of nitric oxide (NO) is restricted by the instability of conventional donors. Here, we develop a facile one-pot method to immobilize S-nitrosoglutathione (GSNO) onto humic acid-coated hydroxyapatite nanoparticles (GSNO-HAs-Fe-HAP NPs). Particle characterization confirms favorable properties for agricultural applications, including prolonged NO release (>6 days) and the mitigation of maize cadmium (Cd) stress. Release test verifies the corelease of humic acid and crop nutrients, while confocal microscopy demonstrates robust NP uptake in maize. Under Cd stress, GSNO-HAs-Fe-HAP outperforms commercial NPK fertilizer, improving photosynthetic efficiency and agronomic traits, reducing grain Cd accumulation by 86%, and upregulating phytochelatins, S-nitrosothiols, and metal transporters (ZmPCR, ZmABCC1, and ZmABCG40). The NP composite reduces ROS accumulation and enhances antioxidant enzyme activity, osmolytes, phenolics, flavonoids, and stress phytohormones. Furthermore, NPs significantly improve soil health parameters and the rhizosphere microbiome. Thus, GSNO-HAs-Fe-HAP is a promising nanofertilizer for prolonged NO delivery and Cd stress mitigation.

title: Canadian evidence-based guidelines on spinal procedures for chronic pain.
abstract: Interventional procedures are commonly used to diagnose and treat chronic pain of spinal origin but guidance on: their indications; frequency; technical conduct; requirements for image guidance; outcome measurement; and management of complications is lacking. These guidelines were developed by a Canadian group of clinicians, researchers, patient partners and representatives from provincial healthcare regulatory and funding bodies. Reviews of published literature were undertaken for commonly performed spinal procedures for pain, and the evidence was synthesised qualitatively. Evidence-based recommendations for each procedure were graded on a scale from A (strongest level) to D (not recommended), or as insufficient (I), using US Preventive Services Task Force criteria with the level of certainty rated as high, medium or low. All consensus recommendations required at least 75% agreement among the guideline panel. Good clinical practice statements were also developed. We provide 15 key recommendations. The guidelines provide clinical practice recommendations and good clinical practice statements for procedures targeting chronic pain originating from the cervical, lumbar spine and sacroiliac joints. Clinical indications, evidence for efficacy and suggested frequency for repeated procedures have also been proposed. These guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations and good clinical practice statements for performing diagnostic and therapeutic spinal interventions for chronic pain.

title: Apolipoprotein E4 and immune dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease: mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that apolipoprotein E4 (APOE4) functions as an organizer of brain-periphery immune crosstalk, coupling maladaptive microglial states with peripheral immune remodeling to establish a self-reinforcing neuroimmune loop that may accelerate the progression of Alzheimer's disease. In the central nervous system, APOE4 pushes microglia away from homeostatic surveillance toward metabolically stressed, inflammatory, and synaptotoxic phenotypes, thereby weakening pathological protein clearance and promoting neurodegeneration. In the periphery, APOE4 primes innate and adaptive immune cells toward a pro-inflammatory state, creating a reservoir that can communicate with the diseased brain and infiltrate it. In addition, APOE4 erodes the separation between central and peripheral immune compartments, enabling bidirectional immune crosstalk that amplifies neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. In this review, we synthesize evidence for APOE4-driven central and peripheral immune dysregulation; discuss therapeutic opportunities for targeting the APOE4 immune axis; and highlight the need for human-derived, longitudinal, cross-tissue studies to identify causal, stage-specific, and targetable immune nodes for precision intervention.

title: Long-term Age- and Region-Specific Changes in Psychiatric Service Utilization Following Japan's First COVID-19 State of Emergency.
abstract: To evaluate nationwide long-term changes in psychiatric service utilization across age groups following Japan's first COVID-19 state of emergency and to compare these changes across regions with different states of emergency intensities. This population-based interrupted time-series study used publicly available aggregated data derived from the National Database of Health Insurance Claims from April 2013 to April 2024, covering nearly all psychiatric patients in Japan. Segmented regression was used to estimate changes after the first state of emergency (April-May 2020). Outcomes were mean daily numbers of psychiatric outpatient visits and inpatient care per 100,000 population. Prefectures were categorized as high-, middle-, and low-intensity regions by the cumulative duration of subsequent declarations. Slope changes in psychiatric outpatient visits varied substantially by age and region. Pre-existing upward trends accelerated after the state of emergency among patients aged 15-39 and 60-69 years, with greater acceleration in high-intensity regions than in middle- or low-intensity regions. The largest change was observed among patients aged 20-24 years in high-intensity regions (0.54 [95% CI, 0.46-0.63]), compared with middle-intensity (0.34 [95% CI, 0.27-0.41]) and low-intensity regions (0.42 [95% CI, 0.34-0.50]). In contrast, psychiatric inpatient care generally declined across most age groups and regions. Following the first state of emergency, psychiatric outpatient visits increased with marked heterogeneity by age group and region, with more pronounced acceleration in high-intensity regions. These findings underscore the value of age- and region-specific monitoring of psychiatric service utilization during future public health crises.

title: Drug-Specific Associations of Angiotensin Receptor Blockers With Parkinson's Disease Risk in a Multicenter Electronic Health Record Cohort.
abstract: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) have demonstrated neuroprotective effects in preclinical models of Parkinson's disease (PD), but individual ARBs differ in pharmacological properties that may influence their neuroprotective potential. Using large-scale hospital electronic health records of the University of California health system, we tested whether specific ARBs are associated with lower PD risk. We conducted a new-user, active-comparator cohort study in the University of California Health Data Warehouse, encompassing 890 712 hypertensive patients across six academic medical centers from 2012 to 2025. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios for individual ARB associations with incident PD, adjusting for demographics, nine preindex comorbidities, and index date. Robustness was assessed through propensity score matching and negative-control analysis. Drug-specific Cox analysis identified irbesartan (HR = 0.588, 95% CI 0.434 to 0.796, p = 0.0006) and olmesartan (HR = 0.797, 95% CI 0.665 to 0.956, p = 0.015) as associated with lower PD risk. Irbesartan survived Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, and propensity score matching supported both associations. In this large multicenter EHR cohort, irbesartan and olmesartan were associated with lower incident Parkinson's disease risk. These findings support further investigation of the renin-angiotensin system as a therapeutic target in Parkinson's disease and may inform the development or repurposing of agents with favorable central nervous system penetration and neuroprotective potential.

title: A Call to Action: Challenges and Future Directions for Sleep Health in Europe.
abstract: Sleep is fundamental to physical, cognitive, and emotional health and wellbeing. However, it is increasingly threatened by environmental, social, technological, and cultural pressures. To identify key priorities for improving sleep health across Europe, the European Sleep Research Society (ESRS)'s Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Committee (EDIC) and Early Career Network (ECN) convened a joint taskforce to review current challenges and develop strategic recommendations. Through a scoping review of the literature, iterative consensus meetings, and collaborative synthesis, the taskforce identified five overarching challenges: (1) environmental and climate-related threats to sleep; (2) inequitable access to sleep medicine and care; (3) the rapid expansion and potential of digital health technologies; (4) widespread sleep misinformation and misconceptions surrounding sleep health; and (5) societal change, constant technological connectivity, and the emergence of a 24/7 culture. These interconnected challenges disproportionately affect vulnerable groups and risk exacerbating existing health inequalities. In response, we propose a coordinated set of recommendations structured according to the PESTEL framework (Political, Economic, Sociological, Technological, Environmental and Legal). Collectively, these recommendations advocate for integrated and equity-focused approaches to strengthen the structural and organisational conditions that support sleep health, improve sleep health literacy, regulate emerging technologies, and ensure that healthy sleep becomes an achievable public health priority across Europe.

title: Neuro-Immune Interactions in the Tumour Microenvironment: Implications for Cancer Progression and Treatment.
abstract: The nervous and immune systems, once viewed as distinct biological networks, are now understood to be closely linked in regulating cancer development, progression, and responses to therapy. Neural structures infiltrate the tumour microenvironment and communicate with immune cells, influencing key processes such as tumour growth, invasion, and metastatic spread. Through neurotransmitters, neuropeptides, and continuous signalling between peripheral tissues and the brain, nerves affect immune cell recruitment, activity, and overall immune balance. Factors including psychological stress, circadian rhythm disturbances, and gut-brain communication further shape antitumour immune responses, highlighting the complexity of these interactions. Research suggests that neuronal signalling not only contributes to cancer-associated symptoms, such as pain, but also affects the efficacy of chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy. Neural biomarkers may provide prognostic value, while interventions targeting neural pathways could strengthen anticancer immunity. Nevertheless, major challenges remain, including cellular heterogeneity, dynamic spatial and temporal interactions, and the limitations of existing experimental models. Continued progress in molecular techniques, bioinformatics, and cross-disciplinary research will be crucial for clarifying these mechanisms. Investigating the neuro-immune-cancer interface offers significant potential for developing innovative treatment approaches that combine neuroscience, immunology, and oncology to enhance patient survival and quality of life.

title: Zona incerta circuits in cognition and the regulation of sleep and wakefulness: potential relevance to Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by progressive cognitive decline and prominent disturbances in sleep and wakefulness, reflecting dysfunction across distributed neural networks. The zona incerta (ZI) is a highly heterogeneous subthalamic structure whose organization is defined by spatial location, molecular identity, neurochemical phenotype, and circuit connectivity. Recent studies demonstrate that distinct ZI cell populations and projections contribute to memory processing, novelty seeking, cortical plasticity, sleep promotion, rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, transitions to wakefulness, and sleep homeostasis. Together, these findings suggest that the ZI is better viewed as a state-dependent subcortical regulatory platform than as a unitary cognitive or sleep center. Emerging pathological evidence further raises the possibility that the ZI may be relevant to neurodegeneration. Amyloid-β deposition has been reported in the ZI of 5xFAD transgenic mice, while experimental tau propagation, human tauopathies other than AD, and studies of other neurodegenerative disorders indicate potential cellular and circuit vulnerability. However, direct evidence from human AD remains lacking, and no study has established a causal pathway from AD pathology to selective ZI dysfunction and subsequent cognitive or sleep impairment. We therefore propose two testable models in which the ZI contributes to AD phenotypes either as a shared circuit node or through parallel, selectively vulnerable functional modules.

title: CAG repeat length shapes bidirectional functional connectome alterations in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3: a multimodal MRI study.
abstract: The ATXN3 gene is the primary driver of brain damage in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3). We aimed to elucidate the patterns of connectome alterations shaped by cytosine-adenine-guanine (CAG) repeat length in SCA3. Eighty-nine genetically confirmed patients with SCA3 and 89 age-, sex-, education-matched healthy controls underwent multimodal MRI and comprehensive clinical assessments. Connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM) was used to identify functional connectivity patterns associated with CAG repeat length. Structural brain damage was assessed using voxel-based morphometry. Mediation analysis was performed to examine the role of structural impairment in connectivity changes. CPM identified a positive and a negative network, whose connectivity strength increased or decreased with CAG repeat length. The positive network (r = 0.397, P < 0.001) was mainly localized within the cerebello-motor circuit and was positively associated with ataxia severity and functional disability. The negative network (r = 0.243, P = 0.022) was distributed across large-scale networks, with selective vulnerability of interhemispheric connectivity, and was associated with motor dysfunction. Besides the canonical motor pathways, limbic-related connectivity was related to motor impairment. Structural analyses revealed widespread gray matter atrophy centered on the cerebellum. Cerebellar atrophy statistically mediated the association between CAG repeat length and connectivity decreases. CAG repeat length is associated with a bidirectional connectopathy in SCA3. Cerebellar atrophy may mediate the connectivity decreases. Future longitudinal studies are required to examine the underlying causal pathway.

title: A critical mechanistic synthesis of PINK1-mediated mitophagy signaling and its therapeutic targeting in Parkinson's disease neurodegeneration.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that is associated with loss of dopaminergic neurons, mitochondrial dysfunction and disruption of cellular homeostasis. PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1) plays a crucial role in mitochondrial quality control by regulating mitophagy, mitochondrial dynamics, and calcium signaling to maintain neuronal bioenergetic homeostasis. This review critically evaluates the molecular pathways underlying PINK1-mediated mitochondrial integrity and the mechanisms by which loss-of-function mutations contribute to the pathogenesis of PD. Familial early-onset PD is strongly associated with pathogenic PINK1 mutations identified through genetic studies. Therapeutic approaches targeting the PINK1 pathway are examined, including adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based gene delivery, direct small-molecule PINK1 activation (MTK458), and indirect modulation of mitophagy and mitochondrial homeostasis by compounds such as curcumin, resveratrol, cannabidiol, gastrodin, and quercetin. Moreover, the complementary restoration of mitochondrial homeostasis through the modulation of downstream targets, such as transcription factor EB (TFEB) activation and BCL2-interacting protein 3-like (BNIP3L/NIX)-mediated mitophagy, is discussed as an indirect therapeutic strategy. Another important finding is that PD is a biologically and clinically heterogeneous disease that requires biomarker-directed and genotype-stratified therapeutic development. Finally, major translational issues are critically evaluated, including challenges related to blood-brain barrier penetration, target specificity, and long-term safety of mitochondrial modulators.

title: Novel acylation modifications in cerebrovascular disease: Molecular mechanisms, crosstalk and therapeutic potential.
abstract: Secondary injury in cerebrovascular disease involves energy failure, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption and neurovascular unit dysfunction. Novel lysine acylations, including lactylation, succinylation, beta-hydroxybutyrylation and crotonylation, have emerged as interfaces through which metabolic changes in lactate, succinate, ketone bodies and short-chain acyl-CoA species are translated into transcriptional regulation and altered protein function. This review organizes the evidence according to a framework that links metabolic donors, writer and eraser enzymes, modification sites, cell types and disease stages. We distinguish relatively developed experimental evidence in acute ischemic stroke and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury from limited findings in haemorrhage and predominantly exploratory evidence in chronic hypoperfusion and vascular cognitive impairment. Proteomic studies have identified 1003 lactylation sites across 469 proteins in rats subjected to cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, although most sites have not undergone causal validation. Comparatively strong evidence has accumulated for sites or regulatory axes involving MeCP2, SOD2, NEK7, ACSL4, PLBD1 and ZO-1. Collectively, current findings indicate that the effects of a given acylation cannot be inferred from its global abundance because they depend on substrate function, cellular origin and the therapeutic window. Major limitations include insufficient site-specific causal evidence, difficulty in directly quantifying crosstalk among post-translational modifications, poor correspondence between animal models and clinical heterogeneity and the absence of effective delivery systems and pharmacodynamic biomarkers. Future studies should integrate spatiotemporally resolved multi-omics, endogenous site editing, cell-specific models, measurable target engagement and independent clinical cohorts to evaluate whether selected acylation sites can progress from experimental candidates to independently validated clinical markers or intervention targets.

title: Comparison of Lateral Decubitus versus Prone Lateral Lumbar Interbody Fusion Using Impact Scores: A Method to Quantify Intraoperative Supply Cost and Variability in Surgery.
journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
abstract: Surgical value metrics report intraoperative supply costs as aggregate institutional dollars, which do not identify which supply categories drive cost. To introduce the Impact Score, each supply category's percentage share of total intraoperative supply cost, as a descriptive framework and, using lateral decubitus (LD-LIF) versus prone lateral (PL-LIF) lateral lumbar interbody fusion as a proof of concept, to determine whether impact scores differ by supply category and align with median-cost rankings, whether exploratory outcome-based value metrics differ between approaches, and whether meaningful inter-surgeon variability exists. Retrospective single-center cohort study at a tertiary center. Seventy-eight single-level L4-5 lateral lumbar interbody fusion cases performed from 2021 to 2026 (32 LD-LIF, 46 PL-LIF). Category-level impact score (percentage of total intraoperative supply cost), supply and total intraoperative cost, exploratory value metrics based on the Oswestry Disability Index and PROMIS-10-derived quality-adjusted life years (including the operative value index and unit price per outcome), and 90-day readmission. Itemized intraoperative supply records were mapped to 33 standardized categories, and each category's impact score was computed as its percentage of total intraoperative supply cost. Time-driven activity-based costing provided staff costs. Category-level impact scores and costs were compared with unadjusted Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. Impact-score and median-cost rankings were broadly concordant. LD-LIF showed higher impact for interbody, screw, biologic, and retractor/dilator, and PL-LIF for neuromonitoring and positioning (all p < 0.01). Navigation and rod did not differ. Total intraoperative cost did not differ between approaches (PL-LIF $17,206 vs LD-LIF $16,404, p = 0.462), nor did staff cost (p = 0.607), and exploratory value metrics did not establish a cost-effectiveness difference, whereas the impact score localized the between-approach difference to supply composition. Biologic impact varied most, with a more than two-fold range among the three surgeons (median approximately 5% to 19%) and higher biologic impact in LD-LIF within individual surgeons. The impact score describes how intraoperative supply costs are distributed across categories. In this single-center, three-surgeon cohort, it identified a potentially modifiable cost driver that neither total cost nor exploratory value metrics revealed. Its use for cross-institutional benchmarking will require a multicenter study of how impact scores vary between institutions with differing vendor pricing and contracting. Because it reflects only the intraoperative phase, it complements, rather than replaces, episode-of-care and outcome-based value assessment. Level III, retrospective comparative study.

title: Twenty-five years of the NIDA clinical trials network and the future of addiction research.
journal: Journal of substance use and addiction treatment
abstract: The National Institute on Drug Abuse Clinical Trials Network (CTN) was established in 1999 to bridge the persistent divide between addiction research and clinical practice through partnerships between researchers and community treatment providers. This editorial examines the evolution of the CTN over its first 25 years and considers priorities for its future. Drawing on the historical development of the Network and articles in this 25-year special collection, we examine changes in the populations and settings represented in CTN research, the incorporation of implementation science, the evolution of community partnerships, the scientific value of accumulated CTN data and experience, and emerging clinical and methodological priorities. Over 25 years, the CTN has developed from a network focused principally on clinically relevant effectiveness trials into a broader national infrastructure for clinical trials and translational addiction research. Its research has expanded beyond specialty addiction treatment programs into primary care, emergency departments, hospitals, community health centers, pharmacies, and other settings in which people with substance use disorders receive care. The Network has also increasingly addressed populations historically underrepresented in addiction research, incorporated implementation questions into clinical research, strengthened community engagement, and used accumulated trial data and emerging analytic methods to generate new scientific knowledge. These developments demonstrate that the value of a clinical research network extends beyond individual trial outcomes. Clinical trials should remain at the core of the CTN's scientific mission. However, trial designs and complementary research methods should be determined by the scientific questions being addressed. The CTN's future impact will depend on its ability to conduct rigorous multisite trials while incorporating implementation, representation, community partnership, and accumulated data and responding rapidly to changes in the drug supply and addiction care environment. These capabilities can help the Network generate evidence that is rigorous, relevant, timely, and more likely to improve addiction care.

title: Altered intrinsic neural timescales in cocaine use disorder.
abstract: Cocaine use disorder (CUD) is a major public health challenge, but its neurodynamic and molecular mechanisms remain unclear despite evidence of structural and functional abnormalities. This study mapped whole-brain intrinsic neural timescales (INTs), reflecting temporal integration of neural activity, using resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging in 44 CUD patients and 44 healthy controls. In the primary analysis with global signal regression (GSR), CUD showed increased network-level INTs in the visual, somatomotor, dorsal attention, frontoparietal control, and default mode networks compared with HC. In the sensitivity analysis without GSR, the visual and somatomotor network differences remained significant. Within the CUD group, regional and network-level INT variation was associated with individual differences in flanker-task performance, despite the absence of significant between-group differences in behavioral performance. Notably, the spatial distribution of INT differences was associated with normative maps of gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptors and the noradrenaline transporter. Atlas-based models showed modest discrimination and limited validation, while outcome-informed cluster-based models yielded higher but exploratory estimates. Importantly, classification performance in a mixed-source evaluation sample was close to chance, indicating limited generalizability. Together, these findings reveal widespread alterations in intrinsic neural timescales in CUD and highlight the relevance of spatiotemporal brain organization to addiction.

title: Should I "stay" or should I "go"? Influence of an anticipated stop on cortical correlates of overground walking.
abstract: Real-world walking frequently requires pedestrians to maintain proactive inhibition to safely navigate unpredictable environments. While cortical modulations occurring during locomotion under environmental uncertainty are well-established, the specific proactive mechanisms underlying this state of inhibitory anticipation remain unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the behavioral and cortical shifts associated with anticipating a stop during overground walking. Fourteen healthy young adults performed fluent and cautious walking tasks with an expected stop. Cortical activity and trunk acceleration were recorded using a 32-channel mobile electroencephalography and an integrated accelerometer. Step-1 latency and step-interval variability were calculated via heel strike detection. Gait-phase-related power modulations were computed, and spectral principal component analysis was applied to attenuate artifacts. The results revealed that cautious walking significantly increased step-interval variability, whereas step-1 latency remained unaffected. At the cortical level, left frontotemporal areas exhibited an attenuated and delayed theta desynchronization during the swing phase. Furthermore, centroparietal regions demonstrated an altered temporal profile of alpha and beta synchronization, characterized by enhanced late-stance synchronization and reduced swing-phase synchronization. The present findings suggest that anticipating a potential stop may alter the rhythmic consistency of gait and reorganize phase-specific cortical dynamics. Being prepared to stop may shift the neural control of automated locomotion toward active monitoring, highlighting the relevance of proactive inhibition during everyday mobility.

title: Ginsenoside Compound K Inhibits Complement C1qA/C3-CR3-Mediated Microglial Synaptic Pruning and Neuronal Pyroptosis.
abstract: Ginseng (Panax ginseng C.A. Meyer), a classic traditional Chinese medicine, has long been used for "calming the mind and enhancing intelligence" to combat cognitive decline. Its major metabolite, ginsenoside compound K (CK), exerts neuroprotection, but the molecular mechanisms against Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain unclear. This study investigated the molecular mechanism by which CK attenuates microglial aberrant synaptic phagocytosis and neuronal pyroptosis via inhibiting the complement C1qA cascade. APP/PS1 mice were used as AD models and treated with CK (20 or 40 mg/kg/d) or memantine (MH, 3 mg/kg/d) by gavage once daily for 14 weeks. Morris water maze and open field tests were used to assess cognitive function and anxiety-like behavior, respectively. HE, Nissl and Golgi staining detected neuronal damage and synaptic integrity. Immunofluorescence and ELISA measured microglial polarization, activation and synaptic phagocytosis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations analyzed the CK-C1qA interaction. Western blot, immunofluorescence and ELISA detected complement components (C1qA, C3, CR3) and pyroptosis-related proteins (NF-κB, NLRP3, ASC, caspase-1, GSDMD-N, IL-18). In vitro cellular experiments, including BV2 cell monoculture and BV2-HT22 transwell co-culture systems, were further performed to validate the causal role of C1qA. CK improved cognitive and anxiety behaviors in APP/PS1 mice, attenuated hippocampal neuronal damage, increased Nissl-positive neurons, restored dendritic complexity and spine density, and upregulated PSD95 and SYP. CK induced microglial M1-like-to-M2-like polarization and reduced Iba1+/CD68+ microglia colocalization with PSD95+ synapses, indicating suppressed synaptic engulfment. CK was predicted to bind to the C1qA globular head domain, reduced C1qA deposition at synapses, inhibited C3, and CR3 expression, suppressed NF-κB phosphorylation, downregulated NLRP3, ASC, cleaved-caspase-1, and GSDMD-N, decreased IL-18 release, and alleviated neuronal pyroptosis. In vitro, CK suppressed C1qA expression in BV2 cells and reduced synaptic C1qA deposition in HT22 cells. CK ameliorated cognitive and synaptic deficits in APP/PS1 mice by inhibiting the C1qA/C3-CR3 pathway to suppress aberrant microglial synaptic phagocytosis and blocking NF-κB/NLRP3/GSDMD-mediated neuronal pyroptosis. These findings elucidate CK's neuroprotective mechanisms and provide scientific evidence for ginseng's traditional cognitive benefits.

title: Investigating Barriers to Clinical Academic Careers Amongst Undergraduate Medical Students.
abstract: There is a critical shortage of academic clinicians in the UK, particularly amongst minority ethnic groups. This study aimed to identify students' perceived barriers to engagement in research, and evaluate whether demographic characteristics influenced these perceptions, in order to identify opportunities to improve training and promote clinical academic careers. A 59-item structured survey was distributed between November 2023-January 2024 to medical students at the University of Cambridge. It incorporated 45 questions using a five-point Likert scale to measure knowledge of research types, confidence with research skills, and understanding of academic careers, producing a total (global) score of 45-225. One hundred and twenty-six students responded. One in four students reported a poor understanding of the clinical academic career pathway. Few students felt confident performing core research steps, such as designing a study (n=23, 18.3%), analysing data (n=27, 21.4%), and writing it as a full research manuscript (n=16, 12.7%). On multivariable analysis, Caucasian ethnicity and year of study were independently associated with increased global scores (betas of 26.4 and 12.5 respectively, both p<0.05), but not sex (beta -0.92, p=0.88). Consequently, students from non-Caucasian backgrounds reported 11.8% less confidence in their understanding of research and clinical academic careers. Students perceive that insufficient understanding, skills and opportunities inhibit their engagement in research. These feelings are heightened in those at early stages of their training and those of non-Caucasian ethnicity. Thus, there is a need for dedicated training delivered early in medical training to increase representation and inclusivity in clinical academia.

title: Mincle exacerbates neuroinflammation and dopaminergic neurodegeneration via synergistic crosstalk with TLR4.
abstract: Microglial activation and subsequent neuroinflammation are critically implicated in the pathogenesis and progression of Parkinson's disease (PD). Macrophage-inducible C-type lectin (Mincle) is a pivotal pattern recognition receptor that participates in the regulation of innate immune responses. Nevertheless, the functional role of Mincle in mediating dopaminergic neuronal injury in PD remains poorly defined. In the present study, we observed a marked upregulation of Mincle expression in microglia in PD mouse models. Pharmacological inhibition of Mincle via Anti-Mincle antibody treatment effectively alleviated LPS-triggered dopaminergic neuronal loss in the SN and rescued motor behavioral impairments in mice. Additionally, Mincle blockade promoted microglial phenotypic transformation, driving a shift from the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. Mechanistically, pharmacological blockade of either TLR4 or NF-κB signaling abrogated LPS-induced Mincle upregulation. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assays further confirmed that the NF-κB/P65 subunit directly binds to the promoter region of the Mincle, verifying that the TLR4/NF-κB signaling serves as a critical upstream regulatory pathway for Mincle expression. Notably, this study provides the first in vivo evidence that Mincle activation by a Mincle-specific agonist trehalose-6,6-dibehenate (TDB) induces robust dopaminergic neurotoxicity and motor dysfunction in C57BL/6 J mice, accompanied by significant elevations in the expression of the pro-inflammatory and microglial activation markers iNOS and CD68. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that synergistic crosstalk between the Mincle-Syk signaling cascade and the TLR4/NF-κB pathway sustains the pro-inflammatory M1 microglial phenotype, thereby triggering progressive dopaminergic neuronal damage in the SN. This study uncovers a previously unrecognized pathogenic role of Mincle in neuroinflammation-mediated neurodegeneration, highlighting Mincle as a promising novel therapeutic target for PD intervention.

title: Identification and whole-genome sequencing of blood-brain barrier-penetrating Riemerella anatipestifer isolated from chickens and ducks.
abstract: Riemerella anatipestifer (RA) is a major cause of bacterial meningitis, which poses a serious threat to the poultry industry. To identify RA strains with a strong ability to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and analyze their genomic characteristics, a co-infection model was established using multiple RA strains with different serotypes in this study. We found that during co-infection with multiple RA strains, certain RA strains rapidly penetrated the BBB and were recovered from brain tissue as early as 0.25 h post-infection. The pioneer strains were selected to further evaluate their BBB-penetrating capacity and pathogenicity in vivo and in vitro. Whole-genome sequencing of three pioneer strains and one RA strain that couldn't penetrate the BBB revealed that these strains had circular chromosomes of 2.14-2.28 Mb, encoding 1,982-2,137 protein-coding genes. All strains carried 40 tRNA genes and 9 rRNA genes, and contained 9-15 genomic islands. Comparative genomic analysis revealed variation in orthogroup composition among the four strains, with strain-specific distributions of resistance genes (24-29 per strain) and virulence genes (4-57 strain-specific genes), alongside variable transposon and IS element profiles. Comparative genomic analysis further uncovered strain-specific distributions of virulence and antibiotic resistance genes, underscoring the genomic plasticity among these isolates. In summary, these findings provide a comprehensive phenotypic and genomic characterization of RA strains with strong BBB-penetrating ability, providing a foundation for future mechanistic studies on RA BBB penetration.

title: Integrating graph attention networks and deep learning with multi-stage computational screening: Bisdemethoxycurcumin as a potent A₂A receptor inhibitor for Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) remains a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with limited disease modifying therapies, as current treatments such as L-DOPA offer only symptomatic relief and are associated with severe adverse effects. This study presents an integrated multi-stage computational pipeline that combines quantitative structure activity relationship (QSAR) modelling enhanced by graph attention networks (GATs), molecular docking, density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and ADMET profiling to identify natural inhibitors targeting four key PD related proteins: adenosine A₂A receptor (A₂AR), gamma aminobutyric acid type A receptor (GABA-A), nuclear factor erythroid 2- related factor 2 (Nrf2), and (α-synuclein). A comprehensive dataset of 1393 structurally diverse compounds derived from 6- hydroxybenzothiazole 2-carboxamide and related scaffolds was assembled and used to train and validate seven regression algorithms. GATs achieved superior predictive performance (R2 = 0.991, Q2 = 0.987, RMSE = 0.487), outperforming Extra Trees (R2 = 0.742), Random Forest (R2 = 0.761), and SVR-RBF (R2 = 0.65). The large dataset size enhanced model generalizability, reduced overfitting risk, and enabled robust feature selection from an expanded descriptor pool of 312 molecular descriptors. Y-randomization with 100 permutations confirmed that all models with meaningful predictive performance were free from chance correlation (ΔQ2 > 0.50), validating the robustness of the QSAR workflow. Molecular docking of six phytochemicals derived from Curcuma longa (ar-turmerone, α -turmerone, bisdemethoxycurcumin) and Salvia officinalis (camphor, 1,8-cineole, α, β-thujone) revealed that bisdemethoxycurcumin BDMC exhibited the strongest binding affinity to the A₂A receptor (-9.1 kcal/mol) among the evaluated phytochemicals. L-DOPA, the current clinical standard of care, displayed weak affinity to the A₂A receptor (-7.2 kcal/mol), consistent with its known mechanism as a dopamine precursor rather than an A₂A ligand. DFT calculations at the B3LYP/6311G(d,p) level showed that BDMC possessed the lowest HOMO- LUMO energy gap (0.1428 eV) and the highest electrophilicity index (ω = 0.1477), indicating superior chemical reactivity and electron accepting capacity. A 200 ns MD simulation confirmed stable BDMC A₂A receptor binding, with 3-8 (mean ≈ 5) persistent hydrogen bonds and no dissociation events throughout the trajectory, as evidenced by centre of mass distance analysis and principal component analysis. ADMET profiling using SwissADME and ProTox II classified BDMC as blood brain barrier (BBB) permeable, compliant with Lipinski's Rule of Five, and safe (LD₅₀ = 2560 mg/kg, toxicity Class 5), compared to L-DOPA (Class 4, LD₅₀ = 1460 mg/kg). Comparative analysis demonstrated that BDMC offers superior predicted binding affinity to the A₂A receptor and a more favourable predicted toxicity profile compared to L-DOPA, positioning it as a compelling A₂A receptor-targeting lead candidate for PD therapy. Collectively, these findings establish a robust computational framework for accelerating drug discovery in neurodegenerative diseases and highlight BDMC as a promising A₂A Receptor inhibitor warranting further in-vitro and in- vivo experimental validation.

title: Artificial intelligence in spatial transcriptomics: a review of methods, datasets, and directions.
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (STs) measures gene expression while retaining the location of transcripts or cells within tissue sections. Unlike bulk RNA sequencing, which averages expression across cell populations, and single-cell RNA sequencing, which generally requires tissue dissociation, ST links molecular profiles to tissue architecture. This spatial information supports the analysis of tissue heterogeneity, cellular organization, and potential intercellular interactions. The spatially resolved nature of ST has unlocked diverse applications in fields such as cancer, neuroscience, reproductive biology, and plant biology. In parallel, the development of publicly accessible databases and repositories has facilitated large-scale, multi-cohort comparisons and benchmarking. The rapid expansion and increasing complexity of these datasets have driven the adoption of machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and artificial intelligence (AI) techniques. These computational tools support a range of tasks, including data pre-processing, image segmentation, spatial domain identification, and pattern recognition. Moreover, they are instrumental in integrative multi-omics analyses and predictive modeling. This AI-focused review provides necessary background on ST technologies and databases and evaluates the use of statistical, ML, and DL methods across the analytical workflow, from image and sequencing-data preprocessing to spatial analysis and LLM-assisted interpretation. We compile key resources related to datasets, AI-driven analytical frameworks, and ST data analysis pipelines, and discuss current challenges, limitations, and future directions for AI-based tools in spatial omics.

title: Glycopyrronium bromide, formoterol fumarate dihydrate and their related compounds with UPLC/PDA-MS for simultaneous determination in pressurized metered-dose inhaler product.
abstract: An ultra-performance liquid chromatography (UPLC) technique with photodiode array-mass spectrometry (PDA-MS) detectors has been developed and validated for the determination of glycopyrronium bromide (GB), formoterol fumarate dihydrate (FFD) and their related substances in pressurized meter dose inhalers. This marks the first time the method has been implemented. Chromatographic analyses have been carried out on a UPLC system with a single quadrupole mass spectrometer (QDa) and a PDA detector. A C18 column has been used prior to the injection valve. The column temperature was set to 40°C. For each analysis, 1 μL of sample was injected at a flow rate of 0.1 mL/minute. The mobile phases used were A (0.5% formic acid in methanol) and B (0.5% formic acid in water). The total run time of the method was 30 minutes. The PDA detector was employed at 215 nm while the mass detector was set to extracted ion chromatography (XIC) mode. The range for detecting impurities of GB was found to be between 0.28 and 0.30 ng/mL, with a limits of 0.92-1.01 ng/mL for quantification. GB and FFD demonstrated linear accuracy. We studied the accuracy of related substances within the limit of quantification value range of corresponding impurities and up to 400% of the limit value. The method we used was linear, rapid, reproducible and accurate. Our proposed method is fast, linear, accurate and reproducible. The UPLC-MS method, which utilized QDa with XIC mode, was developed to ascertain the related substances and assay of GB and FFD.

title: A Chiral Virus-Like Nanoplatform That Broadly Mediates Antibiotic Delivery to the Brain for Bacterial Meningitis Therapy.
abstract: Blood-brain barrier (BBB) preserves brain homeostasis yet restricts therapeutics; in bacterial meningitis, antibiotics' limited penetration impairs delivery to the parenchyma and cerebrospinal fluid, constraining efficacy and motivating strategies to overcome the barrier. To address this, we developed a chiral virus-mimicking mesoporous silica nanostructure (CVSN) functionalized with L-alanine for antibiotic delivery. It offers several distinct advantages: (1) nanoscale dimensions facilitating BBB transport; (2) virus-like morphology enhancing vascular accumulation and penetration, providing a foundation for passive targeting; (3) chiral surface modification conferring active recognition capacity for more efficient biological targeting; and (4) a mesoporous architecture that ensures high drug-loading efficiency and controlled release of drugs. Experimentally, it achieves efficient BBB penetration into the brain parenchyma and shows targeted delivery into microglia and astrocytes. Simulating the loading of cargoes by viruses, it ultimately improves the bioavailability and brain parenchyma and cerebrospinal fluid contents of various antibiotics with distinct physicochemical properties, antibacterial spectrum, and BBB penetration capacity, including cefoperazone, norfloxacin, levofloxacin and imipenem. It helps to treat meningitis induced by both Gram-negative bacteria (e.g., Escherichia coli) and Gram-positive bacteria (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus) and provides a promising avenue to overcome the limitations imposed by the BBB for CNS infections antibiotic therapy in clinic.

title: [Integrated use of ketamine in emergency care].
abstract: Ketamine has emerged as a key drug in emergency medicine in recent years due to its rapid onset of action, hemodynamic stability properties and wide applicability. However, Hungarian regulation still limits its use mainly to anesthetic indications. The aim of this study was to review the literature on the emergency use of ketamine, with particular reference to its role in prehospital and intrahospital analgesia, sedation and rapid sequence intubation (RSI) protocols. A structured literature search was performed in PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library databases, including relevant human studies from 2010 to 2024, and supplemented by selected pre-2010 landmark studies that are pivotal in the historical and clinical context of ketamine use in emergency care. The retrieved publications were thematically categorized, and narrative synthesis was applied. Based on 82 studies reviewed, ketamine was found to be effective and safe in acute analgesia, procedural sedation, agitation management and RSI. Side effects are predominantly mild and well managed. Previous contraindications in patients with head injury are increasingly questioned in the current international literature. The place of ketamine in emergency care is evidence-based. Its use fits well into modern multidisciplinary emergency protocols. It is recommended to update national recommendations in line with international practices. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(42): 1679-1685.

title: Optogenetic cardioversion: To depolarize or to hyperpolarize?
AKAP1 Protects Retinal Ganglion Cells and Preserves Vision by Improving Mitochondrial and Synaptic Health in Glaucomatous Neurodegeneration.
abstract: Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, is characterized by progressive loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and lacks effective neuroprotective therapies. Despite evidence implicating mitochondrial dysfunction in glaucoma, the mechanisms linking elevated intraocular pressure, synaptic dysfunction, mitochondrial failure, and RGC death remain incompletely understood. Here we identify the mitochondrial scaffold protein A-kinase anchoring protein 1 (AKAP1) as a critical regulator of RGC resilience in glaucoma. AKAP1 expression is reduced in glaucomatous retinas and correlates with disrupted mitochondrial dynamics, oxidative stress, synaptic impairment, and visual decline. AAV2-mediated restoration of AKAP1 preserves RGC survival and visual function in two independent experimental glaucoma models. These data suggest that retinal AKAP1 promotes mitochondrial fusion, cristae integrity, and bioenergetic capacity in the inner retina and in stressed cultured RGCs, and is accompanied by increased mitochondrial content in presynaptic terminals of the inner plexiform layer. Retinal AKAP1 is further associated with higher PKA abundance, normalized CaMKII and synapsin phosphorylation, preserved synaptophysin, and lower complement C1q and glial activation markers; these associations do not, by themselves, establish causality. These findings identify AKAP1 as a candidate regulator of mitochondrial and synaptic homeostasis and highlight AAV2-AKAP1 gene therapy as a promising neuroprotective strategy for vision preservation in glaucoma.

title: RNA N6-methyladenosine modifications in plants: molecular mechanisms and biological roles.
abstract: RNA N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modifications dynamically modulate RNA stability, splicing, and translation in plants, influencing developmental and stress response processes. In this review, we provide an overview of the key protein complexes involved in RNA m6A modification, including methyltransferases, demethylases, and m6A-binding proteins. We then demonstrate that m6A modulates vegetative growth, reproductive processes, responses to stresses, and hormone signaling. In agronomically important crops, RNA m6A modifications affect stress resilience, developmental timing, and quality traits, such as drought tolerance, salt resistance, male fertility, pollen viability, and fruit maturation. Furthermore, we elucidate the molecular mechanisms of RNA m6A. Finally, we explore advancements in m6A detection technologies, highlighting emerging trends and future directions. These strategies provide a conceptual framework for moving plant m6A research from descriptive epitranscriptomics toward trait-oriented crop and forest tree improvement.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
abstract: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups. Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows. In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

title: Indirect Echocardiographic Signs of Increased Right-sided Afterload in Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis: Insights from a Multicentre Italian Study.
abstract: Pulmonary vascular involvement is a determinant of worse outcomes in fibrotic lung diseases. Its prevalence and prognostic relevance in patients with progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) is unknown. The aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of indirect echocardiographic abnormalities in progressive pulmonary fibrosis before antifibrotic therapy, characterize a baseline high-risk cardiopulmonary functional profile, and assess 12-month clinical trajectories. Observational, retrospective, multicentre study. 158 patients (median (IQR) age of 71 (65.2-77.0) years) with PPF were enrolled. Thirty (19.0%) had ≥ 1 echocardiographic indirect sign of increased right-sided afterload, 15 (9.5%) ≥ 2, 9 (5.7%) ≥ 3 and 1 (0.6%) all four. A shortened right ventricular outflow tract acceleration time (< 105 ms) was the most frequent alteration (12.7%), followed by right atrial dilation (10.8%). In univariable analysis, ≥1 sign was associated with male sex, a lower DLCO% predicted, a higher FVC%/DLCO% ratio and a shorter 6MWD; in the multivariable model only, male sex remained independently associated (aOR 3.45, 95% CI 0.99-12.07; p = 0.052). Twelve-month FVC trajectories did not differ by baseline echocardiographic status; nonetheless, ≥1 sign was associated with shorter time to acute exacerbation (log-rank p = 0.007) and all-cause hospitalisation (p = 0.001). Echocardiographic signs suggestive of increased right-sided afterload are present in a substantial proportion of PPF patients at the time of antifibrotic initiation. They identified patients at higher risk of acute exacerbation and hospitalisation, regardless of FVC decline. This higher-risk subgroup warrants specific pulmonary vascular evaluation and tighter clinical follow-up.

title: Harnessing the ion transportome to treat cancer.
abstract: Despite significant advances in early detection and therapeutic opportunities, cancer remains a critical global health challenge. The greatest barrier to reducing cancer-associated mortality is the persistent problem of therapeutic resistance and metastasis. Standard treatment approaches, including surgery combined with chemotherapy and radiation, are effective for many patients with localised disease. However, a substantial proportion of patients will experience recurrence and therapy resistance, leading to treatment failure and poor outcomes. This adverse prognosis for patients highlights the critical need to identify new therapeutic targets capable of improving long-term survival. The ion transportome comprises ion channels, solute transporters and pumps that regulate controlled movement of sodium (Na+), potassium (K+), calcium (Ca2+), chloride (Cl-) and hydrogen (H+) across cell membranes. Ion transport is central to many cellular processes, including cell growth, volume regulation, proliferation and migration. In many solid tumours, the finely tuned ionic balance becomes dysregulated, with aberrant expression or activity of membrane transport proteins being closely linked to many of the hallmarks of cancer. Ion channel modulation using pharmacological agents designed to treat channelopathies has demonstrated promise in suppressing cancer progression in preclinical models. Thus, targeting ion-driven vulnerabilities within solid tumours may complement existing therapies to overcome resistance and improve patient outcomes.
