The dynamic nature of ion transport mechanisms means that addressing critical research questions regarding their suitability as pharmacological targets is challenging, highlighting the need to develop innovative approaches to study these processes in oncology.

title: β3-Adrenergic Receptor Agonism Reduces Right Ventricular Systolic Pressure in a Preclinical Model of Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction-Associated Pulmonary Hypertension.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular pharmacology and therapeutics
abstract: PurposePulmonary hypertension (PH) commonly complicates heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), driving morbidity and mortality, yet no therapies exist for HFpEF-PH. β3-adrenergic receptor (ADRB3) agonists may provide cardiometabolic and anti-inflammatory benefits. We evaluated pharmacological ADRB3 modulation in a preclinical HFpEF-PH model.MethodsHFpEF-PH was induced in male and female AKR/J mice via high-fat diet feeding for 16-20 weeks. At 12-16 weeks of feeding, mice were randomized to low-dose mirabegron (LDM, 3.6 mg/kg/day), high-dose mirabegron (HDM, 14.4 mg/kg/day), nebivolol (1.0 mg/kg/day), or vehicle for 4 weeks. A separate cohort received the ADRB3 antagonist SR59230A (0.5 mg/kg/day) or vehicle. Right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP), left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP), body weight change, and gene expression of nitric oxide synthases (Nos1, Nos2, Nos3), thermogenic markers (Ucp1, Ppargc1a), and inflammatory cytokines (Il1b, Il6, Tnf) were assessed.ResultsHDM and nebivolol significantly reduced RVSP compared to controls (P=0.010 and P=1.0×10-4), whereas SR59230A increased RVSP (P=0.006). LDM did not significantly affect RVSP, and LVEDP was unchanged across all treatment groups. HDM also reduced weight gain vs. control (P=0.023). HDM increased Ucp1 and Ppargc1a expression in adipose tissue, and nebivolol increased Ppargc1a expression in adipose tissue. These molecular findings remained significant in sensitivity analyses.ConclusionHDM and nebivolol reduced RVSP in a preclinical model of HFpEF-PH, whereas ADRB3 antagonism increased RVSP. These findings provide pharmacological evidence consistent with involvement of ADRB3 signaling and support further investigation of ADRB3-targeted approaches; the molecular pathways underlying these hemodynamic effects remain to be established.

title: Skeletal muscle transcriptomic profile of older adults with high-impact musculoskeletal pain in the study of muscle, mobility and aging (SOMMA).
abstract: High-impact musculoskeletal pain (i.e., pain that limits daily activities and function) affects a substantial proportion of older adults and is associated with accelerated mobility decline. While skeletal muscle is central to movement and functional capacity, its molecular contribution to pain-related disability in aging remains poorly understood. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from 742 community-dwelling adults aged 70 years or older from the Study of Muscle, Mobility and Aging (SOMMA). Bulk RNA sequencing was performed on vastus lateralis muscle biopsies. Pain impact was classified using self-reported pain and limitations in activities of daily living. Differential gene expression was examined comparing high-impact pain, low-impact pain, and no pain, with sex-stratified analyses. Pathway enrichment analyses were conducted to identify biological processes associated with high-impact pain. High-impact musculoskeletal pain was associated with a distinct skeletal muscle transcriptomic profile, whereas minimal differences were observed between low-impact pain and no pain. Sex-stratified analyses revealed substantial differences in pain-related gene expression for men and women. In men, high-impact pain was characterized by enrichment of musculoskeletal structural and extracellular matrix pathways. In women, high-impact pain was associated with broader transcriptional alterations involving immune, inflammatory, metabolic, and cytoskeletal processes. High-impact musculoskeletal pain in older adults was associated with sex-dependent skeletal muscle transcriptomic signatures distinct from those observed in low-impact pain. These findings implicate muscle-specific molecular pathways in pain-related functional limitations and highlight the importance of sex-informed approaches to understanding and treating chronic pain in aging.

title: Lumbar Facet Joint Morphology and Degenerative Lumbar Spondylolisthesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Study DesignSystematic review and meta-analysis.ObjectivesTo evaluate the associations between lumbar facet orientation, facet tropism, and degenerative lumbar spondylolisthesis (DLS), while assessing sex-specific differences in facet morphology.MethodsA PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261417450). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science were searched through June 2026. Studies evaluating lumbar facet morphology in adults with DLS were included. Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment were performed. Risk of bias and evidence certainty were assessed.ResultsThirty-nine studies met the inclusion criteria. Sixteen studies (3,321 participants) were included in the facet orientation meta-analysis. Patients with DLS demonstrated more sagittally oriented facet joints than controls (SMD 1.30, 95% CI 0.78-1.82; p < 0.0001; I2 = 97.2%). Nine studies (1,913 participants) showed greater continuous facet tropism in DLS patients (MD 2.72°, 95% CI 2.07°-3.38°; p < 0.0001; I2 = 47.2%). Binary facet tropism was not statistically significant (OR 2.20, 95% CI 0.85-5.66; p = 0.0817). Sex-specific, severity, and instability data were insufficient for quantitative synthesis.ConclusionDLS is associated with more sagittally oriented facet joints and greater continuous facet tropism than controls. Limited sex-specific data and heterogeneity highlight the need for standardized measurement techniques and prospective longitudinal studies to clarify causality and sex-related effects.

title: Written exposure therapy augmented with transcranial direct current stimulation for posttraumatic stress disorder: A pilot randomized clinical trial.
abstract: Written exposure therapy (WET) is an evidence-based, trauma-focused psychotherapy for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) that has been tested with several trauma-exposed samples. Although many individuals who receive WET and other trauma-focused psychotherapies experience a significant reduction in PTSD symptoms, there remains room for improvement given that a meaningful proportion of individuals continue to meet the diagnostic criteria following treatment. Adjunctive interventions that can be easily combined with trauma-focused psychotherapies for PTSD may improve treatment outcomes. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is a noninvasive neurostimulation intervention that has demonstrated preliminary evidence of reducing PTSD symptoms. In this study, we combined WET with tDCS to treat PTSD in a pilot randomized clinical trial. Participants (N = 25) received five WET sessions and were randomized to active or sham tDCS targeting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Results showed no statistically significant group differences in PTSD symptom reductions at 1-month follow-up, as assessed using the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 or PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5), ps = .573-.619, and both treatment groups demonstrated significant PTSD improvements, ps < .001, at the final assessment point. However, there was a significant two-way interaction for the PCL-5, p = .010. Deconstruction of this interaction showed that WET with tDCS had an accelerated effect, with larger PTSD symptom reductions occurring earlier in treatment relative to WET with sham tDCS. The findings highlight the potential of tDCS to accelerate PTSD outcomes when combined with WET and support conducting larger randomized clinical trials.

title: Pharmacological Modulation of Catecholaminergic Brain Injury by Dapagliflozin and Its Nanovesicular Formulation in an Isoproterenol Model.
journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
abstract: Sustained β-adrenergic stimulation represents a pharmacologically relevant stressor capable of inducing systemic oxidative and inflammatory injury that extends to the central nervous system. Isoproterenol (ISO), a synthetic catecholamine, is widely used to model catecholaminergic injury in experimental settings. Dapagliflozin, a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor, exhibits pleiotropic antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; however, its effects on catecholamine-induced brain injury remain poorly defined. In the present study, we investigated the pharmacological effects of dapagliflozin and a bile salt-stabilized dapagliflozin-loaded nanovesicular formulation in an ISO-induced model of catecholaminergic brain injury in rats. ISO administration resulted in marked oxidative imbalance, neuroinflammatory activation, behavioral dysfunction, and structural alterations in hippocampal and cortical regions. These changes were accompanied by reduced expression of stress-responsive and neurotrophic proteins, including SIRT6, TRAP1, and BDNF, along with enhanced astroglial activation as indicated by increased GFAP immunoreactivity. Treatment with dapagliflozin attenuated these molecular, cellular, and functional alterations, while the nanovesicular formulation produced a more pronounced improvement of redox balance, suppression of inflammatory responses, normalization of protein expression, and preservation of neuronal architecture and behavior. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that dapagliflozin mitigates catecholaminergic brain injury through attenuation of oxidative and inflammatory stress, with enhanced efficacy achieved via formulation-assisted drug delivery, without implying a distinct pharmacodynamic mechanism.

title: Molecular Signatures of HIV-Induced Neuroinflammation and Neurodegeneration in Human Cerebral Organoids: Identification of Therapeutic Targets for NeuroHIV.
abstract: HIV-associated neurological complications remain a major concern in people living with HIV (PWH), even under effective viral suppression with combination antiretroviral therapy (cART), underscoring unresolved mechanisms driving HIV-related neurodegeneration. To address this gap, we used HIV-1-infected human cerebral organoids (hCOs) containing microglia as a physiologically relevant three-dimensional model of the central nervous system (CNS) and validated key findings in the brain region of simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV)-infected, cART-treated rhesus macaque model. Integrated single-nucleus RNA sequencing with ATAC-seq (multi-omics), identifies cell-type-specific alterations in dual innate immune-driven inflammatory signaling pathways across neural and glial populations in hCOs. Microglia were preferentially infected and activated, initiating IL-17A-mediated cascades involving IFN-γ/STAT1, CEBPB, and NF-κB signaling. These pathways converged with cGAS-STING and Notch-NEURL1 signaling, both associated with neuroinflammation and synaptic dysfunction. cART suppressed viral replication, reduced IL-17A-mediated neuroinflammation, improved mitochondrial function, and restored synaptic gene expression. Collectively, these findings identify dysregulation of IL-17A, STAT1, CEBPB, and cGAS-STING signaling as key molecular drivers of HIV-associated neuroinflammation. They also establish a potential mechanistic link between IL-17A signaling and microglial remodeling, providing a translational framework for the development of CNS-targeted therapies in PWH.

title: PANDAS in the post-COVID era: links to group A Streptococcus and implications for pediatric neuropsychiatry ‒ a narrative review.
abstract: Pediatric autoimmune neuropsychiatric disorders associated with streptococcal infections (PANDAS) are defined by the abrupt onset of tics and/or obsessive-compulsive symptoms temporally linked to group A Streptococcus (GAS). Post-pandemic reports note a rebound of pediatric invasive GAS (iGAS), providing an epidemiologic backdrop for more frequent neuropsychiatric presentations. This narrative review (2020-2025; PubMed/MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Wiley Online Library, MDPI, plus snowballing) synthesizes evidence on the PANDAS/PANS-GAS relationship, clinical spectrum, differential diagnosis with Sydenham chorea (SC), immunopathogenesis, and treatment. Beyond classic OCD and motor tics, the phenotype includes speech disfluency, ocular tics, and acute eating restriction with functional and nutritional risk. Immunologic data support molecular mimicry, Th17/IL-17-driven neuroinflammation, blood‒brain barrier dysfunction, and antineuronal or folate receptor-α antibodies; however, no single validated biomarker exists, and antistreptolysin O (ASO), anti-DNase B document exposure only. Management is individualized and multimodal: antibiotic eradication (with prophylaxis in selected, frequently relapsing cases), immunomodulation (steroids, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), therapeutic plasma exchange) for severe/refractory courses, and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy/Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (CBT/SSRIs) for core psychiatric symptoms. Contemporary data strengthen a post-streptococcal, immune-mediated framework while underscoring heterogeneous case definitions and the paucity of high-quality trials; prospective biomarker and treatment validation remain priorities.

title: Advances in the Anatomy, Histology, and Embryology of the Dromedary (Camelus dromedarius) Brain and Spinal Cord.
abstract: The dromedary (Camelus dromedarius) represents a remarkable model of physiological and anatomical adaptation to extreme environments. While many researchers have focused on its unique metabolic and water-conserving abilities, the neuroscience underlying these adaptations are noticeable unexplored. This study reviews the latest findings in the anatomy, histology, and embryology of the dromedary nervous system. It highlights the gross and comparative neuroanatomy, emphasizing distinctive features of the central, peripheral and autonomic nervous systems, including the complex cerebral vasculature. Histological studies demonstrate a diverse array of neuronal and glial cell types in the caudate nucleus, cerebellum and spinal trigeminal nucleus, reflecting advanced neural processing. Furthermore, embryological investigations trace the development of the nervous system from neurulation and the formation of brain vesicles. Finally, this review connects these neurobiological features to the camel's unique adaptations, such as thermoregulation and pain perception, and discusses the implications of emerging technologies such as nanobody-based therapies derived from camelids for treating neurological disorders. This comprehensive overview underscores the camel as a vital subject for neuroscientific research, offering novel perspectives on neural structure, function and evolution in response to environmental pressures.

title: Single-cell atlas of neuroma-induced DRG remodeling reveals intervention-specific glial and immune programs.
abstract: Peripheral nerve injury caused by cut, crush, or excessive stretch can lead to disordered regeneration and painful neuroma formation. Regrowing axons may terminate in a swollen, hypersensitive nerve stump, producing pain that can outweigh sensory or motor deficits. Despite the frequency of neuromas, treatment outcomes remain inconsistent, and the mechanisms that initiate and sustain neuroma-associated pain are poorly understood. A proximal nerve crush performed upstream of a neuroma or transection may reshape axonal growth and interrupt retrograde injury signaling, potentially promoting a regenerative, pain-resolving state. However, its long-term effects on dorsal root ganglion (DRG) programs remain unclear. Here, we use single-cell RNA sequencing to build an atlas of DRG remodeling after neuroma-forming injury and compare it with two interventions: proximal nerve crush and nerve resection. By resolving transcriptional responses across sensory neurons, satellite glial cells, Schwann cells, and macrophages, we identify intervention-specific glial, neuronal, and immune programs that distinguish regenerative from persistent injury-associated states and nominate pathways that may guide mechanism-based therapies for painful neuromas.

title: Training the Next Generation of Future Surgical Residents: A Scoping Review and Proposal for an Undergraduate Curriculum From the Italian Polispecialistic Society of Young Surgeons.
abstract: The transition from medical school to surgical residency is marked by a persistent gap between theoretical instruction and clinical readiness. In Italy, variability in training programs across centers creates persistent gaps in residents' medical education. Scientific societies are asked to identify current training gaps and define the core competencies required for effective surgical training. We propose an undergraduate curriculum to support last-year medical students in Italy. A scoping review of the literature focusing on structured surgical curricula for undergraduate medical students was conducted. A suggested "curriculum" was introduced at the 2025 Congress of the Italian Polispecialistic Society of Young Surgeons (SPIGC) in Bari, Italy. The SPIGC curriculum includes seven domains: (1) soft skills: communication, informed consent, and interdisciplinary collaboration; (2) clinical and diagnostic skills: outpatient clinic management and perioperative care; (3) hygiene, prevention, healthcare systems; (4) technical skills; (5) emergency and trauma surgery; (6) perioperative management, integrating Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocols, nutritional assessment, and infections; (7) evidence-based medicine and recommendations. The SPIGC curriculum highlights the importance of simulation labs, hands-on workshops, and online learning, while providing clear pathways for fellowships or masters. It also introduces artificial intelligence (AI) systems as a modern learning tool, while highlighting the importance of their safe and responsible use. The SPIGC curriculum may provide a structured plan to improve surgical education for medical students in Italy and to align it with international standards. Its acceptability and impact on training quality and patient outcomes remain to be evaluated through future consensus and prospective studies.

title: Clinical, Cytological, and Virological Factors Associated with Histological Severity and Recurrence in Vaginal Intraepithelial Neoplasia: A Retrospective Observational Study.
journal: Journal of investigative surgery : the official journal of the Academy of Surgical Research
abstract: Vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VAIN) is a rare HPV-related condition with heterogeneous behavior and a relevant recurrence risk. Factors associated with severity and recurrence remain incompletely defined. To explore clinical, cytological, virological, and colposcopic features associated with high-grade VAIN and recurrence. This retrospective study included 42 women with histologically confirmed VAIN at a tertiary center between January 2020 and January 2026. All underwent vaginal cytology, high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) genotyping, colposcopy, and biopsy. Histology was classified as VAIN1 or VAIN2-3. Recurrence was defined as a histologically confirmed lesion after treatment and documented disease-free assessment. Associations were assessed using bivariate and exact analyses. VAIN2-3 was diagnosed in 31 women (73.8%). Among HR-HPV-positive women, HPV16-related infection was more frequent in VAIN2-3 than VAIN1 (65.4% vs 18.2%; OR 8.50, 95% CI 1.27-91.56; p = 0.013). Cytology was associated with histological grade (p = 0.024); all women with HSIL/ASC-H had VAIN2-3, although sensitivity was limited. Over a median follow-up of 24 months, eight women (19.0%) recurred after a median of 11.5 months. HPV16-related infection was more frequent with recurrence (75.0% vs 38.2%; OR 4.85, 95% CI 0.70-54.01; p = 0.112), but the evidence was not definitive. HPV16-only infection showed borderline evidence of association (p = 0.050), while no clear outcome pattern emerged for multiple-genotype infection. No other significant associations with recurrence were observed. HPV16-related infection was associated with high-grade histology among HR-HPV-positive women, while its prognostic relevance for recurrence remains uncertain. The limited sensitivity of cytology underscores the value of multimodal assessment. These exploratory signals warrant prospective validation.

title: Tissue-specific inflammatory responses to systemic LPS in mice with LysM-lineage Hmgb1 deletion.
abstract: Systemic lipopolysaccharide (LPS) exposure induces peripheral inflammation that can engage neuroimmune pathways. High-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) may contribute to peripheral-central communication, but the role of lysozyme M (LysM)-expressing cells in circulating HMGB1 and compartment-specific inflammatory responses remains unclear. Male 7-8-week-old HMGB1 fl/fl LysM-Cre + mice and HMGB1 fl/fl LysM-Cre - littermate controls received LPS (5 mg/kg, i.p.) or saline. Plasma HMGB1, midbrain inflammatory gene expression, cervical lymph node (CLN) transcriptional responses, and choroid plexus CD45 immunoreactivity were assessed at 3 h and 7 days. Spleen, liver, and bone marrow transcriptional responses and Y-maze performance were assessed at 7 days. LPS increased plasma HMGB1 at 3 h and 7 days without significant genotype differences. Despite comparable circulating HMGB1, LysM-lineage Hmgb1 deletion was associated with altered expression of selected midbrain inflammatory transcripts at both time points and with distinct acute and temporal CLN transcriptional responses. At 7 days, splenic responses largely overlapped between genotypes, whereas liver and bone marrow gene-level responses were limited. LPS increased choroid plexus CD45 immunoreactivity at both time points without genotype effects. Y-maze outcomes showed no significant genotype, treatment, or interaction effects. LysM-lineage Hmgb1 deletion is associated with compartment- and time-dependent inflammatory responses following sublethal LPS-induced endotoxemia. The dissociation between plasma HMGB1 and genotype-associated midbrain and CLN responses indicates that total circulating HMGB1 did not fully reflect compartment-specific responses in this model, highlighting the importance of anatomical context in peripheral-central immune signaling.

title: Large cranial windows distort auditory cortical maps and degrade feature integration in secondary auditory cortex.
abstract: Understanding how sensory information is transformed along cortical hierarchies requires reliable measurement of sensory representations across areas. In vivo two-photon calcium imaging through chronic cranial windows has become an essential approach for characterizing cortical sensory representations with cellular resolution and spatial registration across experiments. However, cortical computations, particularly in higher-order cortices, depend on intricate intracortical circuitry and can be sensitive to subtle tissue perturbations introduced during surgical preparation. By comparing sensory maps in the mouse auditory cortex before and after window implantation, we show that commonly used large cranial windows mechanically compress the intrinsically curved cortical surface, producing systematic map distortion away from the window center. Macroscopic and cellular-level analyses further reveal deterioration of feature-selective responses in the secondary auditory cortex following such distortion. Together, these findings identify an overlooked but controllable surgical factor that can bias measurements of sensory representations and highlight an important consideration for reproducibility across studies.

title: Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation boosts evidence accumulation during perceptual decision making.
abstract: Ascending arousal systems, including the locus coeruleus-norepinephrine (LC-NE) system, may shape perceptual decision-making by enhancing sensory processing ("gain") or accelerating response commitment ("urgency"). We examined how arousal-related neuromodulatory activity shapes decisions and whether its effects depend on arousal state. We tested 62 participants in three groups, receiving transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tVNS) at three timings during a random dot motion task. tVNS increased pupil-linked arousal, with early stimulation producing more sustained dilation into decision-making. Behaviorally, tVNS selectively improved accuracy under initially low performance without affecting response times. Drift diffusion modeling linked this improvement to increased drift rate, consistent with more efficient evidence accumulation. These effects occurred across groups but were most pronounced with early stimulation. Our findings support a gain-related enhancement of evidence accumulation under tVNS and suggest that pupil-linked arousal, potentially involving LC-NE among other ascending arousal pathways, may help stabilize attentional engagement when endogenous control is suboptimal.

title: Development and Internal Validation of a Nomogram for Subtherapeutic Total Aripiprazole Concentrations: A Retrospective Real-World Study.
abstract: A straightforward and user-friendly tool for predicting whether the total aripiprazole concentration in a patient falls below 150 ng/mL is currently unavailable. In this study, we identified independent risk factors that influence the subtherapeutic total aripiprazole concentration and developed a nomogram prediction model, thereby providing a reference for individualized dosing. This was a retrospective cohort study that included 409 therapeutic drug monitoring samples. According to established guidelines, the recommended plasma total concentration range for aripiprazole and its active metabolite, dehydroaripiprazole, is between 150 and 500 ng/mL. Therefore, samples with concentrations below 150 ng/mL are classified as belonging to the subtherapeutic concentration group, whereas those within the 150-500 ng/mL range are categorized as the therapeutic concentration group. A multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent factors that affect the subtherapeutic total aripiprazole concentration and a nomogram prediction model was developed. The Net Reclassification Improvement (NRI) and the Integrated Discrimination Improvement (IDI) were employed to assess whether the nomogram model provides statistically significant incremental value over the daily dose-only model. Among the 409 samples, 94 (22.98%) had concentrations below 150 ng/mL. Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that the male (OR = 3.922, 95% CI: 1.732-9.169, P = 0.0012), lower daily dose (OR = 0.525, 95% CI: 0.444-0.608, P < 0.001) and the use of combined valproate (OR = 4.360, 95% CI: 2.013-9.883, P < 0.001) were independent factors affecting the total aripiprazole concentration less than 150 ng/mL. Based on the results, a risk nomogram model was developed to predict the subtherapeutic total aripiprazole concentration. The nomogram showed robust predictive performance, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.916. The concordance index (C-index) was found to be 0.924 based on 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Additionally, the model showed good internal calibration (calibration intercept = 0.00, slope = 1.00, Brier score = 0.088), decision curve analysis indicated favorable clinical utility, with a wide range of threshold probabilities (5-95%). Compared with the daily dose-only model, the full nomogram achieved a NRI of 0.631 (95% CI: 0.305-0.930; P < 0.001) and an IDI of 0.0472 (95% CI: 0.0188-0.0963; P < 0.001). This study established, for the first time, a visualized nomogram model designed to preliminarily predict total aripiprazole plasma concentrations that are below 150 ng/mL. In the future, we will conduct external validation to further evaluate the predictive performance of the model.

title: Efficacy of Medical Treatment Options for Reducing the Risk of Bleeding in Patients With Sporadic and Familial Cerebral Cavernous Malformations: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs) carry a significant hemorrhage risk. While surgery remains the primary treatment, deep-seated or eloquent lesions pose high operative risks, prompting interest in potential pharmacological approaches aimed at lesion stabilization. However, standardized medical management guidelines remain absent. This study evaluates the associations of statins, antithrombotics (ATs), and beta-blockers (BBs) with CCM hemorrhage risk. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO): CRD420251069357), a systematic review of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and Scopus (inception to February 3, 2026) was conducted. Eligible studies compared bleeding outcomes in CCM patients receiving statins, ATs, or BBs versus no medical treatment. A multivariate meta-analysis utilized odds ratios (ORs) and surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) scores to evaluate follow-up (re)bleeding (primary outcome) and hemorrhagic presentation at diagnosis (secondary outcome). Seven studies (n = 3,092) were included. Statin therapy was associated with lower odds of follow-up (re)bleeding versus BBs (OR = 0.32, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.11-0.95) and no treatment (OR = 0.32, 95% CI: 0.14-0.73). Triple combination therapy (statin + AT + BB) was also associated with lower odds of (re)bleeding compared with no treatment (OR = 0.24, 95% CI: 0.06-0.95) and ranked highest according to SUCRA. Statin + AT was associated with lower (re)bleeding odds versus BBs (OR = 0.25, 95% CI: 0.09-0.73). Conversely, BB monotherapy was associated with higher odds of (re)bleeding compared with AT monotherapy (OR = 2.41, 95% CI: 1.13-5.10). Untreated patients had higher odds of hemorrhagic presentation compared with statin + AT (OR = 3.10, 95% CI: 1.31-7.39) and AT monotherapy (OR = 1.86, 95% CI: 1.09-3.13). In the SUCRA ranking, statin + AT had the lowest ranked risk of hemorrhagic presentation at diagnosis. In the absence of established pharmacological strategies, statin- and AT-based regimens were associated with lower CCM hemorrhage odds. However, the available evidence is predominantly observational and limited, with substantial potential for confounding by indication. Together with the null findings of the randomized AT CASH EPOC trial, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and are insufficient to guide clinical practice pending prospective randomized validation.

title: Patch-seq analysis reveals transcriptomic correlates of neuronal firing rate adaptation across subtypes and species.
abstract: Can the transcriptomic profile of a neuron predict its physiological properties? Using a Patch-seq dataset of the primary visual cortex, we addressed this question by focusing on spike rate adaptation (SRA), a well-known phenomenon that depends on small conductance calcium (Ca)-dependent potassium (SK) channels. We first show that in parvalbumin-expressing (PV) and somatostatin-expressing (SST) interneurons, expression levels of genes encoding the ion channels underlying action potential generation are correlated with the half-width (HW) of spikes. Surprisingly, the SK encoding genes are not correlated with the degree of SRA (dAdap). Instead, genes that encode proteins upstream from the SK current, as well as the low-voltage-activated calcium channel, are correlated with dAdap. This general principle is supported by datasets from the mouse primary motor cortex and multiple macaque brain regions. Finally, we generate testable predictions by constructing a minimal computational model.

title: Demographic and clinical factors associated with intraoperative patient cooperation during LASIK.
journal: Medical hypothesis, discovery & innovation ophthalmology journal
abstract: Poor patient cooperation during ophthalmic surgery is demonstrated to result in a variety of complications. The purpose of this study is to evaluate demographic and clinical factors associated with intraoperative patient cooperation during laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) surgery. This retrospective observational study included patients who underwent LASIK at a single institution. Patients were graded intraoperatively by three observers using a 5-point scale for cooperation during flap creation, fixation during excimer laser ablation, and head/body movement, with lower scores indicating better cooperation. Ordinal regression models were used to evaluate associations between cooperation scores and demographic characteristics or medical history. A total of 836 patients were included, with a mean age of 35 years (SD, 10.3; range, 18-80 years), 454 (54.3%) male and 382 (45.7%) female; 70% of patients achieved the best overall cooperation score. Patients were significantly less cooperative during flap creation than during head/body movement (P 0.05); however, anxiety showed an imprecise association with poorer cooperation (OR, 2.20; 95% CI, 0.97 to 5.00). Patient cooperation during LASIK was generally excellent, although cooperation was worst during flap creation. Older age was modestly associated with improved cooperation across all three categories, female sex was associated only with flap-creation cooperation, and longer excimer laser duration was associated with laser fixation and movement, while no statistically significant associations with the assessed medical-history or medication variables were detected. Prospective studies in LASIK and other refractive procedures are warranted to validate and further elucidate the preliminary findings of this study.

title: CB1 receptor inhibition restores synaptoneurosomal alternative splicing landscape in fragile X syndrome mice.
abstract: Fragile X syndrome (FXS), the most frequent heritable cause of intellectual disability and autism, involves impaired cognition and synaptic plasticity. Preclinical studies show that inhibition of the cannabinoid type-1 receptor (CB1R) restores key phenotypic traits in Fmr1 knockout (FX) mice. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain undefined. We analyzed the hippocampal synaptoneurosomal transcriptome and confirmed that synaptoneurosomes are an accurate representation of synaptic composition and function. Then, we analyzed this transcriptome after pharmacological CB1R inhibition in male FX mice and found that rimonabant had limited impact at the gene expression level. Notably, detailed in silico analysis of alternative splicing (AS) revealed that rimonabant reverts numerous AS events in FX mice to wild-type levels. These changes in synaptoneurosomal AS landscape suggest a novel mechanism by which CB1R targeting may restore specific AS patterns. Altogether, our results reveal new molecular alterations in FXS context that are sensitive to pharmacological treatment related to cognitive alleviation.

title: Identification of platelet-derived biomarker in a cohort of Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Evidence has suggested that platelets (PLTs) share biochemical properties with neurons. However, whether PLTs might serve as biomarkers of Parkinson's disease (PD) remains uncertain. In this study, we first analyzed RNA data from a publicly available microarray of the substantia nigra (SN) and RNA-seq data from the PLTs of newly recruited PD patients using weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA). We found that in the SN, the majority of network modules were associated with chromatin organization, energy metabolism, and synaptic signaling, whereas those in the PLTs were related to chromatin organization and DNA metabolism. Potential PLT biomarkers were then screened by comparing the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the significant module pathways with those identified in the SN data by microarray. Additionally, significant genes were identified using genome-wide association study (GWAS) and transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS). The resulting 20 candidate genes were further tested for consistency in single-cell RNA-seq data, followed by assessment using receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) analysis and qPCR validation. The combination of the CRLF3 and LRRC37A2 genes exhibited the best diagnostic performance. Collectively, both PLTs and the SN were common in the chromatin organization pathway, and the diagnostic value of PLT-derived CRLF3 and LRRC37A2 genes deserves further large-scale studies.

title: OGT regulates RNA-binding protein nucleocytoplasmic partitioning, but this fails in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
abstract: O-linked N-acetylglucosamine transferase (OGT) catalyzes the O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) modification to proteins and has been implicated in a range of diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a rapidly progressive and currently incurable neurodegenerative disorder. However, the precise mechanisms by which OGT influences ALS pathogenesis remain largely unresolved. In this study, we used human-induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived spinal motor neurons (hiPSC-MNs), the principal cell type that undergoes degeneration in ALS, to systematically reveal that OGT-related mechanisms regulate RNA-binding protein (RBP) nucleocytoplasmic compartmentalization. Using a combination of antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) technology and small molecular pharmacology, we reveal two distinct regulatory mechanisms of RBP compartmentalization, including by intron-retaining transcript-mediated sequestration and O-linked N-acetylglucosaminylation (O-GlcNAcylation)-mediated nuclear transport. We finally examine the tractability of manipulating OGT activity in the ALS context but demonstrate that the OGT-related mechanisms governing RBP localization in healthy hiPSC-MNs are impaired in the context of ALS-causing VCP and TARDBP mutations.

title: Volume electron microscopy reveals oligodendrocyte axon selection patterns and spatial assembly of myelin and nodes.
abstract: Oligodendrocytes myelinate multiple axons, requiring single cells to coordinate target selection, sheath growth, and node formation across complex cortical geometry. We combined serial block-face electron microscopy, complete segmentation, and three-dimensional reconstruction to analyze early-myelinating oligodendrocytes in the somatosensory cortex of a postnatal day 14 rat at single-cell and nanoscale resolution. Individual oligodendrocytes initiated myelination across all contacted axons, while early ensheathment decreased with increasing process distance from the soma. Each oligodendrocyte also contacted axons within a restricted caliber range, independently of wrapping progression. At prospective nodes of Ranvier, transient cytoplasmic projections extended into axonal domains from adjacent oligodendrocytes and converged near presumptive paranodes. These observations support a structural model in which oligodendrocyte geometry, cell-specific axon selection, and intercellular interactions jointly organize early cortical myelination and nodal assembly, providing testable hypotheses for developmental myelination and repair after demyelination.

title: Thymoquinone-Loaded Hexosomal Nanoparticles Attenuate Neuroinflammation and Improve Cognitive Function in an Alzheimer's Disease Mouse Model.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) involves neuroinflammation that worsens cognitive decline. Thymoquinone (TQ) has potent anti-inflammatory activity, but its therapeutic application is limited by poor solubility, stability, and systemic bioavailability, which may restrict effective brain exposure. This study developed TQ-loaded hexosomal nanoparticles (TQ-HNP) to enhance TQ delivery and therapeutic efficacy in a dizocilpine (MK-801)- induced mouse model of AD. TQ-HNP were prepared using glyceryl monooleate, oleic acid, and poloxamer 407, optimized to ~104 nm size, -31 mV zeta potential, and ~95% entrapment efficiency. Following intraperitoneal administration of free TQ and TQ-HNP, male C57BL/6 mice treated with dizocilpine received intraperitoneal injections of free TQ or TQ-HNP and were subsequently evaluated for cognitive function (Novel Object Recognition test), anxiety-like behavior (Open Field test), and brain levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β. Dizocilpine impaired memory and increased anxiety-like behavior in assessed mice, while TQ-HNP significantly improved both outcomes compared to free TQ. TQ-HNP also reduced IL-6 in the hippocampus and cerebellum and lowered TNF-α and IL-1β in the cerebellum, confirming its anti-inflammatory efficacy. TQ-HNP enhanced the brain delivery of thymoquinone, mitigated neuroinflammation, and restored cognitive function in the AD-like mouse model, supporting its potential as a nanocarrier-based therapeutic strategy for Alzheimer's disease and other neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Effect of a Subanesthetic Dose of Esketamine on Postoperative Sleep Disturbance After Oocyte Retrieval Under Intravenous Anesthesia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Postoperative sleep disturbance (PSD) is a common complication after oocyte retrieval under intravenous anesthesia. This study aimed to evaluate whether a subanesthetic dose of esketamine reduces the incidence of PSD. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial included 196 women undergoing oocyte retrieval under intravenous anesthesia. Participants were randomly assigned to the esketamine or control group. During anesthesia induction, the esketamine group received an intravenous bolus of esketamine 0.2 mg/kg, whereas the control group received an equivalent volume of normal saline. The primary analysis was conducted according to the intention-to-treat principle, with missing outcome data handled using multiple imputation; 189 participants (95 in the control group and 94 in the esketamine group) were included in the per-protocol sensitivity analysis. The primary outcome was the incidence of PSD on postoperative day (POD) 3, defined using a composite criterion of an Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS) score ≥6 or a numerical rating scale (NRS) score ≥6. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of PSD on POD 1, postoperative pain scores, postoperative anxiety and depression scores, and patient satisfaction with the anesthetic technique. In the intention-to-treat analysis with multiple imputation, the estimated incidence of PSD on POD 3 was lower in the esketamine group than in the control group (13.06% vs 24.90%; risk difference, -11.84 percentage points [95% CI, -22.98 to -0.69]; relative risk [RR], 0.52 [95% CI, 0.28-0.99]; P = 0.047). The per-protocol (PP) sensitivity analysis yielded similar results (12.8% vs 24.2%; RR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.28-0.99]; P = 0.043). PSD on POD 1 did not differ between the groups. No between-group differences in postoperative anxiety or depression scores were noted. Postoperative pain scores at 30 minutes were significantly lower in the esketamine group (P < 0.001). Dreaming was more frequent in the esketamine group (21.4% vs 11.2%; P = 0.048), and the time to full alertness (12 [10-14] vs 11 [9-13] minutes; P = 0.002) and postanesthesia care unit (PACU) stay (34 [30-37] vs 31 [29-34] minutes; P = 0.005) were modestly longer. A single subanesthetic dose of esketamine was associated with a lower incidence of short-term PSD on POD 3 in women undergoing oocyte retrieval under intravenous anesthesia. Larger multicenter studies are warranted to confirm these findings. China Clinical Trial Registry Identifier: ChiCTR2500105998.

title: Computational identification of phytochemical NMDAR pore-targeting candidates for radiation-induced cognitive decline.
abstract: Radiation-induced cognitive decline (RICD) is a major late complication of cranial radiotherapy, particularly in pediatric brain tumor survivors. Memantine, an uncompetitive N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) channel blocker, provides clinically relevant neuroprotection, However, the development of additional NMDAR-targeting candidates with favorable CNS penetration and pharmacological properties remains an unmet need. An integrated computational workflow was used to prioritize phytochemical NMDAR pore-targeting candidates. The memantine-bound NMDAR structure (PDB ID: 7SAD) guided pharmacophore modeling and virtual screening of 17,967 IMPPAT phytochemicals, followed by drug-likeness and CNS pharmacokinetic filtering. Prioritized compounds were evaluated by molecular docking, MM-GBSA/MM-PBSA, triplicate membrane-embedded molecular dynamics (MD), residue-contact and pore-geometry analyses, PCA/FEL, DFT, and in silico toxicity prediction. Filtering yielded 14,491 drug-like compounds, 1429 pharmacophore hits, 77 docking/MM-GBSA candidates, and seven compounds for detailed analysis. Triplicate 100 ns membrane simulations revealed ligand-dependent differences in binding energetics, interaction persistence, conformational sampling, and pore geometry. Dehydrocrenatidine (IMPHY010917), Skimmianine (IMPHY007265), Dehydrocrenatine (IMPHY007797), and Vasicinol (IMPHY004852) showed the most compelling complementary profiles, although no single compound consistently ranked highest across all descriptors. Dehydrocrenatidine, Skimmianine, Dehydrocrenatine, and Vasicinol are prioritized as putative NMDAR pore-targeting phytochemicals for RICD. Their complementary energetic, interaction, and conformational profiles provide a basis for experimental evaluation of NMDAR inhibition, CNS exposure, and radiation-relevant neuroprotection. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40203-026-00763-9.

title: Isolation of Hymenolepis diminuta cysticercoids for therapeutic use: The need for fully disclosed methodology.
abstract: Helminth therapy holds considerable theoretical promise for clinical and public health applications. Unfortunately, clinical trials have often used helminths produced using methods that are both highly variable and insufficiently described in the literature, which may hinder reproducibility and troubleshooting. This study aimed to devise a method for purification of helminths that avoids mechanical filtration, which may damage some organisms. In particular, the goal was to devise a method to separate large quantities of cysticercoids of the cestode species Hymenolepis diminuta (HDCs), a process that has not been described previously but that would be necessary before HDCs can be used clinically. The physical size and behavior of HDCs in solution were assessed and used to create a patented washing device. The cross-sectional area of HDCs varied over a 10-fold range, from approximately 0.06 to 0.6 mm 2, dependent in large part upon the host. That cross-sectional area correlated in a linear fashion with the steady-state speed of HDCs while falling through solution, which varied over a 5-fold range, from approximately 0.4 mm/s to 2.0 mm/s in the solution tested. These parameters were used to develop a washing device that utilized a variable flow speed dictated by changing column diameter and an upward flowing column of liquid that effectively and simultaneously suspended HDCs of various sizes in a wash solution. This study describes a detailed method of purification of HDCs, organisms that could potentially be used for helminth therapy. It is hoped that government agencies or non-profit organizations can use such technology to conduct rigorous clinical trials, potentially leading to the production of reasonably priced therapeutics.

title: Alcohol use is common in older patients with fall-related fractures: a secondary analysis from a prospective cohort study using PEth as an objective assessment of consumption.
abstract: Alcohol increases the risk of falls and complications, but data on alcohol intake among trauma patients is unreliable. Excessive alcohol use can contribute to excess frailty and confusion in frail individuals and increase fall risk in otherwise robust older people. Phosphatidylethanol (PEth) is a biomarker accumulating through repeated alcohol intake, i.e., suitable for screening long-term consumption. Our primary aim was to describe alcohol consumption in older individuals admitted after a fall-related fracture. Our secondary, exploratory aims were to investigate the association between alcohol, frailty, and short-term clinical outcomes in these individuals. This prospective observational cohort study included those ≥ 65 years admitted due to acute fall-related fracture February 1, 2023-August 31, 2024. PEth was taken at admission. Predefined norm values classified low/no consumption as 0.30 µmol/L. Frailty status was assessed by the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS). Our secondary aim was addressed using multivariable logistic regression on a propensity score-matched cohort. Of the 505 patients included, 13% had PEth indicating hazardous consumption, 8.9% intermediate consumption, and 78% had low/no consumption. Of the non-frail patients, 18% had hazardous and 11% intermediate consumption. 19% of all women and 29% of all men had continuous alcohol consumption (defined as PEth ≥ 0.05 µmol/L). In the matched cohort, alcohol consumption was associated with a higher odds ratio (OR) of hyponatremia (OR 2.3, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.1-4.5, P = 0.02). A trend towards lower odds of 90-day mortality (OR 0.2, CI 0.1-1.0, P = 0.05) was seen. A minimum of 1/5 older patients with fall-related fractures have continuous alcohol consumption. Non-frail patients had a higher intake than frail individuals. Alcohol consumption was associated with higher odds of hyponatremia. Otherwise, no apparent negative effects were identified in the short term.

title: Whole-Food Protein Sources Differentially Modulate Postprandial Plasma Dileucine Profiles in the Post-Exercise State.
abstract: Dileucine, a leucine-containing dipeptide, may enhance anabolic signaling more than leucine alone. This study examined postprandial plasma dileucine and leucine concentrations after ingesting animal- and plant- whole foods and their association with muscle protein synthesis rates (MPS). Secondary analysis was performed on plasma samples collected from two randomized controlled trials totaling 26 healthy adults (25 ± 4.3 y). Participants consumed low-fat pork (LFP), high-fat ground pork (HFP), complementary rice and beans (COMP), an iso-nitrogenous mixed nutrient beverage (ISO), or a carbohydrate control (CHO). Plasma concentrations and MPS was measured. Plasma dileucine increased significantly only after LFP ingestion (p < 0.05), with a greater 300-min iAUC compared to CHO (p = 0.038). Plasma leucine increased in all conditions except COMP and CHO with LFP demonstrating the highest concentrations (p < 0.05). A modest correlation was observed between dileucine Cmax and the change in MPS (ΔMPS; r = 0.436, p = 0.037), whereas leucine Cmax showed no significant association (r = 0.265, p = 0.102). Whole-food protein sources generally do not elevate plasma dileucine, except for LFP. While dileucine Cmax correlated with ΔMPS, the strength of this relationship suggests dileucine is likely one of several postprandial factors influencing MPS beyond free leucine.

title: Examining the roles of socioeconomic status and relevant health correlates (body mass index, diet quality, and inflammation) for neuropsychological function in young adults.
abstract: In this cross-sectional analysis, we examined associations between socioeconomic status (SES), body mass index (BMI), inflammation, diet, and cognitive performance. While low SES is associated with lower cognitive scores, the present study investigated whether these variables - specifically BMI, inflammatory biomarkers, and dietary intake - statistically mediate this relationship. The final sample included 109 young adults (mean age = 21.31; 65% female; 45% white). Analyses utilized a comprehensive neuropsychological battery, including the NIH Cognitive Toolbox and Kaufman Brief Intelligence Test, alongside biomarkers of inflammation (Interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α)), and self-reported dietary intake via the National Cancer Institute's Diet History Questionnaire - Third Edition. A pre-registered analysis using bootstrapped standard errors across 5,000 bootstrapped replications in 'lavaan' tested whether (i) associations between SES and executive functioning and episodic memory were statistically mediated by a higher BMI and (ii) associations between BMI and executive functioning and episodic memory were statistically mediated by elevated inflammation and sugar or fat intake. BMI did not account for the association between SES and cognition; however, BMI, fat intake, and sugar intake were inversely correlated with cognitive functioning. Sugar intake mediated the association between BMI and cognition, though this finding was not significant after adjusting for covariates. Inflammation did not mediate the relationship between BMI and cognition. These results provide support for a link between BMI and cognitive performance and preliminary evidence of a mediating role of sugar intake. Further longitudinal and experimental research is needed to extend these findings and characterize underlying mechanisms.

title: Vascular dementia and vascular cognitive impairment-current treatments and future prospects.
journal: International journal of stroke : official journal of the International Stroke Society
abstract: Vascular cognitive impairment (VCI) and vascular dementia (VaD) represent a substantial and growing global health burden, yet remain under-recognized and comparatively under-researched. Two broad categories are post-stroke cognitive impairment, and VCI secondary to chronic cerebrovascular disease of which the most common cause is cerebral small vessel disease (SVD). In addition, cerebrovascular pathology frequently coexists with Alzheimer's disease (AD), increasing the probability that AD pathology will manifest as clinical dementia. Current management focuses primarily on prevention through modification of cardiovascular risk factors and lifestyle interventions. Intensive blood-pressure control has shown the strongest evidence, reducing future all-cause dementia while slowing progression of white-matter abnormalities. Multidomain lifestyle interventions incorporating exercise, diet, cognitive training, and vascular risk monitoring may also preserve cognition, although results across trials remain variable. In established VCI and VaD, treatment options are limited; cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine lack convincing evidence of benefit, and no pharmacological therapy has definitively demonstrated symptomatic improvement or delayed disease progression. Advances in understanding SVD and VCI pathophysiology are, however, identifying promising therapeutic targets. Emerging evidence highlights endothelial dysfunction, impaired cerebral autoregulation, increased blood-brain barrier permeability, inflammation, and glymphatic dysfunction as possible mechanisms underlying SVD. Current trials are evaluating treatment approaches based on this framework including cerebral vasodilators such as cilostazol, isosorbide mononitrate and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors, anti-inflammatory therapies, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, remote ischemic conditioning, and strategies targeting glymphatic function. Improved mechanistic understanding, appropriately targeted interventions, and adequately powered long-term clinical trials are required to translate these emerging approaches into effective treatments for VCI and VaD.

title: Genetic Insights Into Cryptogenic Stroke: From Etiologic Heterogeneity to Clinical Translation.
abstract: Cryptogenic stroke remains challenging because its complex etiology and limited diagnostic tools hinder precise secondary prevention. Growing genetic evidence suggests that cryptogenic stroke may have identifiable genetic architectures that provide additional insights into etiologic classification. In recent years, large-scale genome-wide association studies, multi-omics integration, and other genetic investigations have begun to reveal signals linked to several potential causes, including occult atrial fibrillation and atrial cardiopathy, nonstenotic carotid artery plaque, patent foramen ovale-related paradoxical embolism, monogenic disorders, clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential, and cancer-related thrombosis. These findings suggest a possible shift from exclusion-based diagnosis toward a more mechanism-driven approach. Recent genetic discoveries have enabled preliminary work on predictive models for risk stratification. Emerging genetic tools may also offer promising approaches for etiologic stratification and mechanistic investigation. However, current research in this area remains limited by heterogeneous definitions, modest sample sizes, limited ancestral diversity, and gaps in mechanistic and prognostic evidence. Consequently, clinical translation remains at an early stage. Future research should establish larger and more diverse genomic cohorts with longitudinal phenotyping and advance multidimensional data integration. These efforts may refine etiologic classification and support precision treatment in cryptogenic stroke.

title: Precision Oxygen Modulation in the Reperfusion Era: Conditioning and Therapeutic Strategies in Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) and advanced perfusion imaging have transformed acute ischemic stroke (AIS) treatment, yet tissue hypoxia may persist because of delayed presentation, incomplete reperfusion, microvascular no-reflow, and secondary injury. Oxygen is an essential substrate for cerebral metabolism and a modifiable therapeutic exposure; however, clinical studies of oxygen-based interventions have yielded inconsistent results because of heterogeneity in timing, dose, delivery, and patient selection. Here we propose precision oxygen modulation (POM) as a stage-, phenotype-, and tissue-informed framework for the reperfusion era-treating oxygen exposure as a dose-titrated therapy that must be matched to the right patient, time window, physiological target, and safety boundary. POM integrates oxygen conditioning strategies that may prime neurovascular resilience before or around ischemia, time-limited therapeutic oxygen strategies deployed around reperfusion to support tissue at risk, and recovery-stage strategies paired with rehabilitation. We synthesize clinical and preclinical evidence linking oxygen tension to excitotoxicity, oxidative stress, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and repair, while emphasizing the context-dependent risks of hyperoxia. We outline an operational decision framework and translational roadmap based on phenotype- and imaging-guided selection, biomarker validation, protocolized dosing, predefined safety boundaries, and phenotype-enriched randomized trials. POM is presented as a testable translational framework for organizing heterogeneous evidence and guiding the prospective validation of stage-specific oxygen modulation in modern stroke care.

title: Medical assistance in dying on psychiatric versus somatic grounds: survey on the experiences of relatives.
journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science
abstract: Relatives are often intimately involved in medical assistance in dying (MAID) on both psychiatric and somatic grounds. Greater insight into the extent to which certain experiences occur in practice will help physicians provide support. To investigate how relatives of patients who received psychiatric versus somatic MAID scored on measures of opinions and emotions regarding the MAID trajectory; involvement in the trajectory; and judgement of the due care criteria. We included 616 Dutch relatives (18 years and over) of patients who received psychiatric or somatic MAID, recruited via an online cross-sectional survey conducted in the Netherlands between April 2023 and February 2025. Survey distribution occurred via social media, pamphlets, a patient federation and newspapers. In total, 110 participants had experienced psychiatric MAID and 506 somatic MAID. Outcomes included the following: opinions about the duration of the MAID trajectory; emotions due to MAID (five-point Likert scale); involvement in the MAID trajectory (five-point Likert scale); judgement of the due care criteria (five-point Likert scale); and total Empathy Questionnaire score (a validated scale). Following psychiatric MAID, gratitude, resignation, relief and sadness were most strongly felt (mean 3.5-4.2 on a scale from 1 to 5). More than 25% felt insufficiently involved in the MAID trajectory, and more than 80% positively judged the due care criteria, with no differences between psychiatric and somatic MAID. Respondents who experienced psychiatric MAID felt greater powerlessness (p = 0.026, 95% CI [-1.082, -0.069]) and guilt (p = 0.004, 95% CI [-0.833, -0.166]), and more often found the MAID trajectory too long (68.3 v. 21%, p < 0.001, U = 37 118, z = 9.19). Relatives of people who received psychiatric MAID generally reported positive experiences that did not differ from those with somatic MAID. In regard to psychiatric MAID, relatives experienced greater powerlessness and guilt, emphasising the importance of relative involvement and support. Future research should investigate how this involvement can be optimised.

title: A randomised controlled feasibility trial of FREED-Mobile, a smartphone-friendly decision-making tool, designed to facilitate help-seeking in young people with eating disorders.
abstract: Early intervention increases the likelihood of eating disorder recovery but many young people delay help-seeking. We developed a smartphone-friendly, online decision-making tool to address this gap (FREED-Mobile (FREED-M)). To conduct a randomised controlled feasibility trial of the FREED-M decision-making tool with 16- to 25-year-olds with a suspected eating disorder and no previous treatment for this. Participants were randomly allocated to FREED-M or an active control in a parallel group, two-arm trial. Outcomes were measured at weeks 0 (baseline), 4 (post-intervention) and 12 (follow-up). The primary feasibility outcome was attrition at follow-up. Other outcomes included motivational, clinical and economic measures. We over-recruited with 204 randomised participants (including 20 fraudulent participants). Main analyses were conducted with 184 genuine responders (FREED-M: n = 91, control: n = 93). At baseline, participants' mean age was 21.0 (s.d. 2.0) years, 89% identified as female and 64% as White. Mean body mass index was 23.1 kg/m2 (6.3). N = 83 participants had an anorexia nervosa-like disorder, 101 had another eating disorder or high eating disorder risk. Attrition at week 12 was n = 112 (61%). Of the n = 42 FREED-M participants who provided acceptability ratings, 79% liked the intervention and 66% found it useful. Between-group effect sizes for motivation and readiness to change were small to medium at 4 weeks (d = 0.27 and d = 0.15, respectively) favouring FREED-M, but differences were not sustained at follow-up (d = -0.02 and d = -0.12, respectively). Although the attrition rate was high, recruitment exceeded expectations. Acceptability of FREED-M was high among participants who provided acceptability ratings. Motivation/readiness to change and help-seeking are candidates for primary outcomes in a future randomised controlled trial.

title: Clozapine, suicide prevention and risk perception in psychiatry.
abstract: Clozapine remains the most effective treatment for treatment-resistant schizophrenia and one of the few psychiatric medications consistently associated with reduced suicidal behaviour. Nevertheless, its use remains markedly limited despite advances in pharmacovigilance, haematological monitoring and individualised prescribing strategies. This editorial examines whether psychiatry may continue to evaluate clozapine through historically inherited models of risk perception that emphasise treatment-attributable mortality while insufficiently incorporating the lethality of severe mental illness itself, particularly suicide. Clozapine therefore represents not only a psychopharmacological treatment, but also a revealing case study in how psychiatry conceptualises competing forms of mortality.

title: Ethnic disparities in time to bipolar disorder diagnosis: retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Lithium is a first-line maintenance treatment for bipolar disorder yet delays in diagnosis and lithium initiation remain common. This retrospective cohort study examined whether time to bipolar disorder diagnosis and lithium initiation differ by ethnicity, gender or age among 88 patients at South London and Maudsley National Health Service Foundation Trust. Delay outcomes were non-normally distributed and log-transformed before analysis. No demographic characteristic was significantly associated with time to lithium initiation. Ethnicity was significantly associated with diagnostic delay, with individuals from minority ethnic groups experiencing longer delays than White individuals (median 556 v. 50.5 days; IQR [89.8, 1342] v. [6.25, 222]), which persisted after adjustment for age, gender, substance use and illness severity, and remained robust to outlier removal. Although social deprivation was not accounted for, these findings suggest possible systematic diagnostic inequities in bipolar disorder, calling for culturally informed diagnostic practices and further investigation in larger, multi-site samples.

title: Animal models for investigating post-stroke cognitive impairment: A neurovascular trafficking perspective.
abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a major cause of long-term disability after ischemic stroke, yet its mechanisms remain incompletely explained by infarct volume, lesion location, or conventional vascular risk factors alone. Animal models are indispensable for clarifying how ischemic injury evolves into delayed cognitive dysfunction and for determining which mechanisms are experimentally tractable, reproducible, and translationally relevant. This review examines PSCI from a neurovascular trafficking perspective, focusing on how laboratory animal models can be used to investigate secretory pathway stress, endolysosomal dysfunction, autophagy-lysosomal flux, extracellular vesicle signaling, blood-brain barrier disruption, glial reactivity, myelin debris clearance, white matter injury, and cognition-relevant behavioral phenotypes. Rodent models of transient or permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion, photothrombotic stroke, embolic stroke, chronic cerebral hypoperfusion, bilateral carotid artery stenosis, and subcortical white-matter injury each reproduce selected components of the human PSCI spectrum. No single model fully captures the temporal, vascular, cellular, and cognitive complexity of human PSCI; therefore, model selection should be driven by the mechanistic question, disease phase, vascular pathology, cellular compartment, cognitive domain, and welfare burden under investigation. The central argument is not that neurovascular trafficking failure is already a proven causal pathway, but that well-designed animal studies can test, refine, or falsify this hypothesis. Future studies should integrate model validity, translational rigor, and welfare refinement through longitudinal cognitive testing, multimodal imaging, cell-specific molecular profiling, extracellular vesicle phenotyping, intervention-based validation, randomization, blinding, sample-size justification, humane endpoints, perioperative care, and transparent reporting.

title: Metabolomics workbench: data-driven classification and correlation analysis between metabolite classes, biomarkers, and drugs.
abstract: Public repositories now accumulate an unprecedented amount of metabolomics data. Despite the opportunities for large-scale meta-analyses opened by these repositories, the deposited data rarely becomes systematically re-analyzed. We conducted a systematic metadata-based re-analysis of all human blood metabolomics studies in the Metabolomics Workbench performed using Orbitrap or QTOF mass spectrometry, encompassing 44 165 samples. After harmonizing metabolites with PubChem identifiers and embedding them using SMILES representations, we generated a map of 6752 blood metabolites forming 25 structural clusters, and subsequently performed correlation analysis between these clusters, biomarkers, and drugs. Analysis of 337 120 metabolite pairs detected in at least 10 studies showed that structurally related clusters display correlated abundances (ρ up to 0.6). Correlation patterns among established clinical biomarkers revealed candidate metabolic correlates, several with ρ > 0.7. We also developed open-source software enabling similar analyses for any metabolite across the Workbench data explored. Additionally, curating drug-containing datasets enabled meta-analyses for compounds such as acetaminophen, metoprolol, and atenolol, identifying both known and novel metabolic signatures. Besides the biological insights, we have found that Orbitrap and QTOF tend to detect different metabolites, but they give quantitatively coherent results on overlapping compounds. Overall, the present study provides the methodology and software to perform large-scale mining of public metabolomics data enabling its re-analysis to obtain novel biomedical insights.

title: Temporal brain dynamics and fluid reasoning after extreme prematurity.
abstract: Extremely preterm (EPT) birth (<28 weeks' gestation) disrupts brain maturation and increases later neurodevelopmental and mental health vulnerability. Temporal irreversibility quantifies directional brain dynamics, capturing the temporal organization of brain function. We examined whether EPT birth alters temporal irreversibility at 10 years and its association with cognition at 12 years. Resting-state functional MRI was acquired at 10 years of age in 33 children born EPT and 26 term-born controls. At 12 years of age, 29 children born EPT and 21 term-born controls underwent cognitive assessment using the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children-Fifth edition (WISC-V). Temporal irreversibility was quantified globally, across large-scale functional networks (visual, somatomotor, dorsal attention, salience, limbic, control, and default mode [DMN]), and at the node level using the INSIDEOUT framework. Children born EPT showed reduced temporal irreversibility globally and in higher-order association networks (control and DMN, P < 0.01; dorsal attention and salience, P < 0.05). Node-level analyses identified two association-network parcels that remained significant after false discovery rate correction (left precuneus and right dorsomedial frontal cortices). Within the EPT group, fluid reasoning was the only WISC-V domain significantly associated with temporal irreversibility, with higher global irreversibility associated with poorer fluid reasoning. These findings may inform future neurodevelopmental monitoring and intervention strategies after prematurity.

title: Special Issue on the 41st Annual Meeting of the International Society for Traumatic Stress Studies: Frontiers in Traumatic Stress.
abstract: At the 41st Annual Meeting of the International Society for Traumatic Stress Studies, held in Baltimore, Maryland, on September 17-20, 2025, researchers and practitioners worldwide convened to examine issues central to the theme, "Frontiers in Traumatic Stress: Global Perspectives and Creative Solutions." The meeting highlighted global and local complexities in trauma assessment, intervention, and policy and showcased innovative research and practice across diverse contexts. This editorial spotlights papers drawn from presentations at the meeting that illuminate key innovations, emerging developments, and evidence-based practices across the field. The featured work spans topics including the recognition of chronic trauma exposure across global settings; promises and challenges posed by advances in digital technologies and artificial intelligence; progress in trauma-informed assessment, diagnosis, and intervention; and community-based approaches addressing the impacts of systemic trauma. This issue presents a curated sample of the meeting's compelling presentations to illuminate the depth and breadth of contemporary trauma innovations and to chart directions for future research, clinical practice, and policy that more holistically support improved outcomes for affected individuals and the prevention of trauma-related psychopathology following exposure.

title: Protein disulphide isomerase protects against ALS/FTD phenotypes associated with cyclin F in zebrafish and cellular models.
journal: Redox report : communications in free radical research
abstract: Mutations in CCNF, encoding cyclin F, cause a small proportion of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) cases. Mutant cyclin F mislocalises from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, impairs the ubiquitin proteasome system, disrupts endoplasmic reticulum (ER) to Golgi transport, and triggers ER stress and apoptosis. Protein disulphide isomerase (PDI), a redox-active ER chaperone of the thioredoxin superfamily, protects against ALS phenotypes induced by mutant SOD1, TDP-43, and FUS, but its activity against mutant cyclin F has not been examined. To test whether PDI overexpression prevents the cellular and behavioural phenotypes induced by the ALS/FTD-associated cyclin FS621G mutation. Neuro-2a cells were co-transfected with mCherry-tagged wild-type or mutant cyclin FS621G and V5-tagged PDI or empty vector. Subcellular localisation, XBP-1 and CHOP activation, proteasome reporter (GFPu) accumulation, nuclear morphology, and cleaved caspase-3 immunoreactivity were assessed by confocal microscopy. Transient transgenic zebrafish larvae generated by mRNA co-injection of cyclin F and PDI were assessed by photomotor response at 48 h post-fertilisation. Mutant cyclin FS621G induced cytoplasmic mislocalisation, ER stress (assessed by XBP-1 and CHOP activation), proteasome dysfunction (indicated by GFPu accumulation), and apoptosis (assessed by nuclear condensation and caspase-3 activation), all of which were significantly attenuated by PDI co-expression. Zebrafish larvae expressing cyclin FS621G swam significantly shorter distances than uninjected or wildtype controls, and co-expression of PDI restored motor function to near-wildtype levels. PDI protects against ALS/FTD-associated mutant cyclin F in both cellular and in vivo zebrafish models, identifying PDI as a redox-based therapeutic target for CCNF-linked ALS/FTD.

title: Effects of prucalopride on anxiety and depressive symptoms among constipated patients: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Prucalopride, a 5-HT4 receptor agonist, has shown potential for rapid anxiolytic and antidepressant effects in preclinical studies. This meta-analysis aims to evaluate changes in anxiety and depressive symptoms after prucalopride treatment in chronically constipated adults. A systematic search of PubMed, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, ClinicalTrials.gov, and reports from the Food and Drug Administration and European Medicines Agency was conducted from inception to 1 March 2026. Included studies were double-blind randomized controlled trials originally designed to assess effectiveness in treating chronic constipation in adults. As preplanned, the primary endpoint was the change in anxiety and depressive symptoms. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) were pooled and analyzed using a random-effects model. This study is registered with PROSPERO, number CRD42024602454. Five randomized controlled trials, including 2,404 participants, were included. The meta-analysis revealed a significantly greater improvement in anxiety and depressive symptoms derived from quality-of-life scores with prucalopride compared with placebo in the random-effects model (SMD = -0.19, 95% confidence interval [CI] [-0.3117; -0.0707]; P = 0.0019; I2 = 52%). Improvement in anxiety and depressive symptoms was associated with improvement of constipation, but not with the daily dose of prucalopride. All studies were rated as having some concerns for biais in selection of the reported result. Prucalopride improves anxiety and depressive symptoms in chronic constipation. Further studies are needed to explore the potential repurposing of prucalopride for anxiety and depressive disorders.

title: Glioblastoma immune landscape remodeling following treatment with CD70-targeted CAR-T cells.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has shown limited efficacy in glioblastoma (GB), largely because of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We have previously demonstrated that the ligand-based mCD70-directed construct mCAR27 specifically eliminates CD70⁺ GB cells in vitro, and induces durable tumor remission with prolonged survival in a syngeneic model of orthotopic GB. Despite the therapeutic promise of CD70 as a GB CAR-T cell target, the impact of CD70-directed CAR-T cells on the brain tumor immune landscape after target interception remains unexplored. Here, we independently confirmed a tumorigenic role for CD70 in murine GB by performing bulk RNA sequencing and in vivo experiments. Next, we applied single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) to decipher the transcriptome of GB-infiltrating immune cells in immunocompetent mice bearing CD70+ GB after intratumoral mCAR27 therapy. CAR-T cell treatment expanded adoptively transferred cells and was associated with increased endogenous Cd8⁺ T-cell infiltration, alongside a reduction in immunosuppressive populations, including Tregs and anti-inflammatory M2-like macrophages, but also subsets of dendritic and natural-killer cells. CD70 expression was detected on multiple GB-infiltrating immune subsets, notably Tregs and M2-like macrophages. Transcriptionally, mCAR27-mediated GB remission led to a coordinated downregulation of type-I interferon-stimulated genes and immunosuppressive mediators such as Arg1, Tgfbi, Cd274, Pdcd1lg2 and Lag3, coupled with upregulation of genes involved in inflammatory resolution, findings consistent with attenuation of GB-derived inflammatory stress and immunosuppression. Collectively, we showcase that CD70-directed CAR-T cell therapy remodels the post-treatment immune landscape towards resolution of inflammation and reduced immunosuppression, supporting sustained immune surveillance.

title: Comorbid asthma - occurrence and associations with patient-related outcomes in COPD: a cohort study.
journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
abstract: Clinical features of COPD and asthma overlap, complicating differential diagnosis. This study investigated the prevalence of comorbid asthma in COPD patients and its association with patient-related outcomes. Patients with a doctor's diagnosis of COPD were randomly selected in two cohorts 2005 (n = 1060) and 2014 (n = 1671), from primary and secondary care in Sweden.
